Job Description Summary
GE Vernova is one of the world's leading energy technology companies, helping to electrify and decarbonise the planet. Within our Power Transmission business, our UK team is at the forefront of delivering high-voltage gas insulated switchgear (GIS) solutions to some of the most critical infrastructure projects across Great Britain. Driven by a step-change in our market position following the launch of our next-generation low-carbon GIS technology, we are experiencing significant growth and are now looking for a Lead GIS Project Manager to join our team in Stafford.

Job Description
The Role

This is a senior individual contributor role within a high-performing team of project management professionals, working at the intersection of commercial delivery, customer relationships, and cross-functional collaboration. You will take ownership of a portfolio of high-value GIS projects from contract award through to warranty close-out, acting as the primary point of contact between GE Vernova, its manufacturing facilities in France and Switzerland, and UK-based customers including transmission system operators and engineering, procurement and construction contractors.

Your projects will typically run over three years, encompassing engineering, manufacturing, site installation and commissioning phases. At any given time, you can expect to manage a portfolio of around eight to ten concurrent projects, with individual contract values reaching up to $80 million USD. This is a role where your decisions carry real commercial weight, and your ability to manage risk proactively, build trust with customers, and keep complex programmes on track will be central to your success.

Key Responsibilities:
• Managing a portfolio of GIS projects end to end, from post-order handover through to warranty completion, ensuring delivery against programme, budget, and quality commitments.
• Acting as the primary commercial and contractual interface between GE Vernova, the customer, and our manufacturing supply chain and ensuresing that projects follow execution execution best practices and company policies.
• Maintaining accurate and up-to-date project data in portfolio management tools, including scheduling, billing plans, risk registers, and variation orders.
• Preparing and presenting quarterly project management reviews, covering financial performance, risks, opportunities, and progress against milestones.
• Identifying, assessing, and managing project risks and opportunities, escalating issues appropriately and proposing mitigating actions. Capturesing, analysingzes and sharinges lessons learned throughout the project.
• Coordinating installation and commissioning activities on UK construction sites, including pre-site safety planning, subcontractor management, and site visits (minimum quarterly Gemba walks per project).
• Ensuring subcontractors meet GE Vernova and customer EHS requirements, and that method statements and risk assessments align with contractual obligations.
• Managing non-conformance reports and customer complaint workflows to resolution, ensuring snagging items are closed out prior to project handover.
• Supporting factory acceptance tests (FAT) at our manufacturing sites, facilitating effective communication between customers and the factory teams.
• Driving commercial outcomes including the identification and management of variation events under NEC3 , NEC4 and NEC4FIDIC contract terms.

Essential Requirements:
• Extensive experience in project management, ideally gained in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment within the infrastructure, energy, utilities, or high-voltage electrical sector.
• Demonstrable ability to manage project risk, cost performance, and commercial outcomes independently and to a high standard.
• Strong commercial acumen and experience working under formal contract frameworks, with working knowledge of NEC3 or NEC4 and FIDIC terms being particularly valuable.
• Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to build credible relationships with customers, contractors, and internal teams alike.
• Willingness and ability to travel periodically within the UK for site visits and customer meetings, and internationally (approximately four times per year) to our manufacturing facilities in France and Switzerland.
• A valid UK driving licence and passport.

Nice-to-Have Qualifications:
• A background in or knowledge of high-voltage switchgear, substations, or related electrical power products.
• Experience working in or alongside the energy transmission or distribution sector, whether in a project delivery, engineering, or commercial capacity.
• Familiarity with project portfolio management tools such as Smartsheet, Planisware, or similar.
• A project management qualification such as PRINCE2, PMP, or equivalent.
• Prior experience with SAP in a project delivery context.
• Understanding of UK Construction Design and Management (CDM) regulations and their application on infrastructure sites.

What We Offer

GE Vernova exists to power a world that works. Our technology helps generate around a quarter of the world's electricity, and the work happening right here in Stafford is a direct part of that story. This role offers genuine variety and commercial responsibility, within a collaborative team that is number one in the UK market for next-generation, low-carbon GIS technology.

Beyond the base salary itself, we offer:
• An annual bonus scheme based on financial and personal performance.
• Flexible working arrangements, including a compressed work week.
• A competitive defined contribution pension, with employer contributions that can be flexed to suit your needs.
• Private medical insurance, with comprehensive family cover available.
• 26 days annual leave, with the option to buy or sell up to four additional days, plus bank holidays.
• Life assurance at above-market levels.
• Group income protection, paying a proportion of your salary for up to five years if you are unable to work due to illness or injury
• Access to GE Vernova's FlexChoice flexible benefits programme, allowing you to personalise your package — including dental cover, critical illness insurance, a cycle to work scheme, a lifestyle account, and more.
• Access to digital learning, leadership development programmes, and genuine career mobility across a global business.

GE Vernova is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals and are committed to building a workforce that reflects the diverse communities we serve.

Additional Information
Relocation Assistance Provided: No

Job Description
Lead Network and Cybersecurity Engineer
Candidates who possess most of the experience outlined below and demonstrate strong motivation to develop expertise in the remaining areas are strongly encouraged to apply. We recognize the multifaceted nature of this role and value both proven experience and a genuine commitment to professional growth.

Role Purpose
This is a technical engineering role, operating as a key contributor within the project team to ensure the successful execution of secure network and cybersecurity solutions. As an experienced practitioner for HVDC Control and Protection, you will contribute to the technical implementation of Network and Cybersecurity standards, drive quality in secure architectural design, and support the broader engineering team. Working across global projects involving multiple stakeholders, you will own the delivery of specific workstreams, from design and configuration to testing and commissioning of digital control and Substation Automation Systems. You will serve as a reliable technical resource, ensuring that project delivery meets our high standards of security, reliability, and quality.

Leadership and Impact
Technical Implementation: Serve as a key contributor for Network and Cybersecurity domains. You will execute technical designs, validate design choices, and ensure alignment with global standards across project tasks.
Collaborative Delivery: Foster a culture of technical rigor. You will collaborate with peers and provide guidance to junior engineers, acting as a supportive team member in complex engineering environments.
Stakeholder Communication: Translate technical requirements into actionable project tasks. You will facilitate dialogue between internal teams and external suppliers, ensuring clear communication regarding technical progress and security requirements.
Risk and Quality Management: Proactively identify project-level technical risks and assist in driving resolutions. Implement improvements in engineering processes and maintain adherence to established Network and Cybersecurity best practices.
Decision Making: Operate with a high degree of independence on assigned work packages. You are empowered to make technical decisions within defined project parameters and escalate to senior leads when high-stakes challenges require additional expert input.

Key Responsibilities
Design and Architecture: Execute the design of secure networks and communication architectures, adhering to IEC 62443-3-3 principles. Build and maintain functional infrastructure (Networking, virtualization, server OS configuration).
Compliance and Lifecycle: Ensure consistent adherence to Secure Deployment Guides and Security Assurance Plans. Execute vulnerability monitoring, patch management, and disaster recovery processes.
Technical Oversight: Implement IP address strategies, perform substation-level hardening, and evaluate Network and Cybersecurity solutions from 3rd party suppliers.
Tendering and Regulatory Support: Support bidding processes with knowledge of regulations such as EU NIS, NERC, and BDEW; assist in mapping requirements between varying Network and Cybersecurity standards.
Operational Execution: Perform design, configuration, and testing to meet project budgets and schedules. Assist in FAT (Factory Acceptance Testing) and execute on-site installation and commissioning of LAN networks.
Documentation: Ensure all technical documentation aligns with engineering policies and procedures, including appropriate confidentiality levels.

Qualifications and Experience
Technical Foundation: Demonstrated expertise in Industrial Networking, Systems Architecture, or Cybersecurity. Relevant technical knowledge gained through a degree in a related field OR equivalent industry-recognized certifications (e.g., GICSP, ISA/IEC 62443, CCNA/CCNP).
Domain Expertise: Experience in industrial control and protection system design, specifically within Distributed Control Systems and Substation Automation (IEC 61850 environments).
Cybersecurity Standards: Applied knowledge of IEC 62443 standards (parts 4-1, 4-2, 3-3, 2-4) and hands-on experience with firewalls (Fortinet), IDS (Nozomi, Radiflow), VPN/PKI, and endpoint security.
Networking: Strong knowledge of Layer 2 and 3 protocols (IPv4, OSPF, VRRP, LACP, SNMP, SSH, SFTP). Ability to build functional infrastructure.
Systems and Infrastructure: Experience with virtualization (VMware, HyperV, Proxmox) and Windows Server configuration.
Industrial Protocols: Proficient in IEC 101/104, PTP, OPC UA, DNP3, Modbus TCP/IP and diagnostic debugging using Wireshark.
Product Familiarity: Experience with GE Reason, Westermo, or Meinberg products is advantageous.

Additional Information
Relocation Assistance Provided: No

Job Description Summary
GE Vernova's Rotating Machines Rugby operation builds some of the most technically demanding equipment in defence, aerospace, and industrial power. When a product leaves our facility, it must perform — and the integrity of that performance starts here, on the shop floor.

This is a senior technical leadership position at the heart of a low-volume, high-complexity manufacturing environment where bespoke engineering and exacting safety-critical standards define everything we do.

As Lead Quality Assurance Engineer, you will serve as the primary technical authority for manufacturing quality within the RMR Quality team. This is not a process-administration role, you will provide hands-on operational leadership on the shop floor, drive the transition from reactive issue management to proactive defect prevention, and hold firm accountability for the quality integrity of high-value, bespoke equipment.

You will be the operational anchor for the Quality function — the person who determines when our processes are truly production-ready, and who sets the standard for technical rigour across Manufacturing, Engineering, and Project Management.

If you are an experienced quality leader ready for genuine technical ownership in a mission-critical engineering environment, we want to hear from you. You must also be a sole British citizen (hold a valid UK passport) with the ability to obtain UK security clearance to SC-level.

Job Description
Operational Quality Leadership

• Direct daily Quality Engineering and inspection activities, aligning resource prioritisation with manufacturing schedules, customer commitments, and safety-critical compliance requirements
• Act as the primary operational authority for the Quality function, interfacing directly with Manufacturing, Engineering, and Project Management to resolve technical bottlenecks
• Lead daily operational reviews, monitor workload and technical risk, and ensure clear escalation of issues that threaten quality integrity

Quality Engineering & Non-Conformance Management

• Provide hands-on leadership for NCR management, ensuring all investigations, dispositions, and corrective actions are technically sound and fully supported by empirical evidence
• Lead high-stakes root cause investigations for complex product failures, driving permanent, systemic preventive actions rather than temporary containment measures
• Enforce strict accountability for CAPA effectiveness across all functional owners, eliminating repeat defects through process-based solutions

Quality Performance & Continuous Improvement

• Manage operational performance through advanced trend analysis (Pareto, defect rates, Cost of Poor Quality), translating data into targeted improvement initiatives
• Champion the development and maintenance of manufacturing Control Plans and PFMEAs, working with Engineering to improve process capability and reduce variability across complex production lines
• Facilitate structured improvement projects using Lean/Six Sigma methodologies to enhance quality systems, inspection efficiency, and digital process controls

Quality Governance & Cross-Functional Alignment

• Ensure full compliance with ISO/AS9100 standards and customer specifications, maintaining the integrity of all quality records, inspection evidence, and non-conformance documentation
• Lead operational preparation for internal, customer, and regulatory audits, ensuring follow-up actions are closed with technical rigour
• Maintain clear functional boundaries, ensuring the Quality team provides expert assurance and technical support without diluting the accountability of Manufacturing and Engineering

What You Will Bring 
Essential
• Proven technical leadership in a complex, highly regulated manufacturing environment — aerospace, defence, power generation, or a comparable bespoke engineering sector
• Deep expertise in NCR management, structured root cause analysis (8D, Ishikawa), and CAPA effectiveness verification
• Practical experience applying PFMEA, Control Plans, and APQP including PPAP
• Strong technical literacy: ability to interpret complex engineering drawings, tolerances, GD&T, and detailed technical specifications
• Demonstrated experience using SAP and digital QMS systems for quality data management and reporting
• Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills — able to translate complex technical quality issues into clear, actionable language for both technical and non-technical audiences
• Proven ability to coach, develop and upskill quality and production teams, embedding a culture of continuous improvement and quality ownership at every level
• Strong MS PowerPoint and Excel skills for analysis, reporting and presenting quality performance data to senior stakeholders
• You must also be a sole British citizen (hold a valid UK passport) with the ability to obtain UK security clearance to SC-level.

Job Description Summary
Every major project starts with a question no one wants to answer blindly: Should we bid, and at what risk? As a Lead Project Planner at GE Vernova, you are the person who answers that question with evidence.

You will build the probabilistic schedules that give our leadership the confidence — or the caution — to make multi-million-pound bid decisions based on quantified data, not instinct. Your work directly shapes which projects GE Vernova pursues, how they are priced, and how confidently they are delivered.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who brings deep technical scheduling expertise together with genuine commercial and risk awareness. If you find precision satisfying and uncertainty worth solving, this role was built for your strengths.

Job Description
What You Will Do
• Build and own bid-stage schedules — develop fully scoped, resource- and cost-loaded schedules aligned to the Bill of Materials (BOM) / Statement of Work (SOW), with no scope gaps and full compliance with DCMA (Defense Contract Management Agency) 14-point health criteria.
• Drive probabilistic analysis — apply three-point estimating and quantitative risk analysis (including Monte Carlo / QRA methods) to produce a defensible, risk-adjusted cost and schedule position that informs bid/no-bid and pricing decisions.
• Maintain bi-directional traceability — link schedule activities to RAID (Risks, Assumptions, Issues, Dependencies) risk references and maintain estimated time impacts throughout the bid phase, ensuring no data is lost at handover.
• Lead the ITO-to-execution transition — validate the bid schedule against final contracted scope, support formal baseline approval, and hand over the baselined schedule and associated RAID data to the Project Controller with a clear, structured briefing.
• Support change control during execution — re-engage when material schedule variance arises to construct What-If scenarios, quantify critical path impact, float consumption, and Extension of Time (EoT) entitlement without modifying the approved baseline.

What You Bring
You are someone who combines analytical rigour with strong communication skills — equally comfortable interrogating a schedule logic network and presenting risk findings to bid leadership.
Required
• Significant experience building and maintaining complex, resource-loaded project schedules using enterprise tools such as Planisware, Primavera P6 (P6), or equivalent.
• Strong working knowledge of Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) / Cost Breakdown Structure (CBS) development and alignment between planning tools and ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) / financial systems such as SAP.
• Practical experience with schedule health diagnostics, including DCMA 14-point analysis.
• Solid understanding of probabilistic risk techniques — three-point estimating, Expected Monetary Value (EMV), and Monte Carlo / Quantitative Risk Analysis (QRA) methods — and their application to contingency and margin decisions.
• Understanding of Earned Value Management (EVM) principles and how schedule integrity underpins performance measurement baseline (PMB) accuracy.
• Demonstrated ability to engage effectively across Commercial, Risk, Cost Engineering, and project leadership teams.
• Must hold, or be eligible to obtain, SC Clearance
Preferred
• Experience working in a bid or ITO (Invitation to Offer) environment within complex systems or capital projects delivery.
• Familiarity with change management processes, including What-If scenario modelling and the distinction between rebaselining and re-time-phasing.

Education
A formal qualification in Project Management, Engineering, or a related discipline is beneficial, but we are most interested in your total experience and professional achievements.

GE Vernova is a purpose−built global energy company, helping customers electrify and decarbonise the world. Our Power Conversion & Storage business works with customers across oil and gas, metals, mining, and heavy industry, delivering drives, controls, automation, solar, and battery energy storage solutions – as well as long−term service and upgrade programmes for existing installations.

This role sits at the heart of that growth ambition. You will directly lead a team of six sales professionals, set the direction for how we develop and win business across the segment and region, and personally engage at senior levels with key customers and partners. The territory spans the UK and Northern Europe, with a particular focus on expanding our presence in the Nordics.

Key Responsibilities:
• Lead and develop a team of sales managers and business development professionals, setting clear direction, individual plans, and performance expectations.
• Drive segment revenue growth in line with the annual operating plan, with a target of approximately $50M across Industry and Oil & Gas.
• Build and maintain senior−level customer relationships, identifying and converting strategic opportunities across new and existing accounts.
• Define and execute the segment's go−to−market strategy, including Scandinavian market development.
• Shape compelling value propositions by aligning customer requirements, market trends, and GE Vernova's full product and service portfolio.
• Manage and develop the opportunity pipeline using Salesforce, ensuring accurate forecasting and reporting.
• Collaborate closely with internal stakeholders including operations, commercial, and second−line account management to ensure full coverage of the installed base.
• Champion GE Vernova's values and standards across safety, quality, integrity, and customer focus.

Essential Requirements:
• Proven experience leading a commercial sales team in an industrial or energy−related environment.
• A background selling technically complex equipment or solutions – either into oil & gas, metals, mining, or heavy industry, or selling comparable products (such as drives, controls, switchgear, or power electronics) into industrial markets.
• Technical credibility sufficient to engage confidently with engineering and procurement stakeholders – whether gained through formal qualification or extensive industry experience.
• Strong commercial acumen, including pipeline management, value-based selling, and competitive positioning.
• Good understanding of the oil & gas market segment.
• Demonstrable experience using a CRM platform (Salesforce experience is a strong advantage).
• A valid driving license and passport, with the ability to travel across the UK and Northern Europe (up to approximately 20-30% of working time).

Nice-to-have qualifications:
• Degree in electrical engineering, automation, controls, or related discipline.
• Direct experience with power conversion products such as variable frequency drives or industrial automation systems.
• Familiarity with Scandinavian markets, customers, or business culture.
• Lean or Six Sigma certification.

We believe the work we do matters – and we want the people who do it to thrive. Here is what you can expect when you join GE Vernova in the UK:
• A performance-based bonus under GE Vernova's sales incentive plan, rewarding delivery against your targets.

• Access to FlexChoice, GE Vernova's flexible benefits programme, giving you the ability to tailor your package each year to suit your personal needs.
• A defined contribution pension scheme, with a competitive employer contribution through the Pension Saver plan.
• Comprehensive family private medical cover (inpatient, outpatient, and diagnostic), with the option to flex your level of cover.
• 26 days annual leave, with the option to buy or sell days through FlexChoice.
• Life assurance at above-market levels, with flexibility to increase cover.
• Group income protection, providing a proportion of your salary for up to five years if you are unable to work due to illness or injury.
• A Lifestyle Account – GE Vernova contributes £60 and matches your contributions up to £300 per year, which you can put towards fitness, wellbeing, or personal development.
• Digital learning resources, leadership development programmes, and on-the-job growth opportunities.

Job Description
Machine Learning Engineer
Global’s central Data Science function is recruiting a Machine Learning Engineer to work across our data and product portfolio.
As a Machine Learning Engineer at Global, you’ll be part of the engineering bridge between data science and production—taking models built by our data scientists and making them robust, scalable and maintainable across audience targeting, advertising measurement and content intelligence. You’ll work with colleagues across Data Science, Machine Learning Engineering and Data Engineering, bringing your own ideas to how we build and improve our models. The role is based in central London (Holborn, with occasional travel to Leicester Square).
Key Responsibilities
• Model Productionisation, Serving & Lifecycle Management (70%): Take models built by our data scientists and turn them into reliable, testable production systems; build the serving infrastructure to deliver them across batch and real-time use cases; build and maintain consistent feature pipelines; keep models healthy once live through monitoring, drift detection and periodic retraining; and help audit and migrate existing models to modern standards without disrupting live products.
• Standards & Enablement (15%): Apply and contribute to the engineering standards for how models are built, tested and deployed, aligned to the MLOps platform; help create reusable templates and documentation that enable data scientists to work independently; and feed your experience back to help shape the platform direction.
• Cross-functional Partnership (15%): Work with Data Science, MLOps, Data Engineering and Product to understand new products early and ensure models are handed off in a deployable, maintainable form.
What You’ll Love About This Role
• Think Big: This is a true AI and data-driven space—the models you ship influence what millions of listeners hear and how brands invest their media budgets.
• Own It: You’ll take ownership of getting models into production and keeping them healthy, and your voice will count in how we build going forward—not just maintaining what exists.
• Keep it Simple: You’ll build on and contribute to reusable patterns and templates rather than one-off solutions.
• Better Together: You’ll work with Data Science, MLOps, Data Engineering and Product, with plenty of opportunity to broaden your experience across Global’s data products.
What Success Looks Like
In your first few months, you’ll have:
• Built a working understanding of Global’s engineering and data science tools and how they connect.
• Established strong working relationships with Data Science, MLOps and the wider engineering team.
• Contributed to the audit of existing ML models in production, assessing stability, maintainability and risk.
• Taken a model (or part of one) to a more robust, documented state, and contributed reusable components others can use.
What You’ll Need
• Production ML experience: You’ve delivered ML projects in a commercial environment, contributing to deployment, CI/CD and lifecycle management. You’ve delivered models across different mediums, such as batch models running on a schedule and models served via APIs.
• Strong Python: Solid Python written to production standards: you unit test your code, use version control and code review as a matter of course, and code defensively so that simple edge cases don’t break production environments. Experience with PyTorch or similar ML frameworks is a plus.
• Model evaluation & monitoring: You can investigate why models underperform across data, features and architecture, and explain the trade-offs behind your choices. You understand how to monitor models in production, detect model and data drift, and put safeguards in place to defend against it.
• Orchestration: Familiarity with workflow orchestration tools such as Airflow or similar, and an understanding of how to schedule, monitor and maintain dependable data and model pipelines.
• Real-time ML & reproducibility: A good understanding of production inference patterns and reproducible environments (Docker, MLflow or equivalent), and a willingness to deepen it.
• Cloud & data tooling: Familiarity with a SQL data warehouse-style system, and experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP or Azure. Experience with AWS, including SageMaker, Snowflake and Kubernetes is a plus.
• Engineering mindset: A focus on reliability, maintainability and continuous improvement, with an appetite to learn from more experienced colleagues and share what you learn.

Who we are…

GlobalData operates an intelligence platform that empowers leaders to act decisively in a world of complexity and change.

By uniting proprietary data, human expertise, and purpose-built AI into a single, connected platform, we help organisations see what’s coming, move faster, and lead with confidence.

Our solutions are used by over 5,000 organisations across the world’s largest industries, delivering tailored intelligence that supports strategic planning, innovation, risk management, and sustainable growth.

Why join GlobalData?

GlobalData is at a pivotal point in its growth journey, and we need curious, ambitious, courageous people to support us in achieving our vision to deliver intelligence that transforms uncertainty into opportunity for the world’s most successful organisations.​

Our big ambitions mean that life at GlobalData is fast-paced, entrepreneurial and rewarding. Working together in an intellectually challenging environment, where learning is super-charged to keep us on our toes, the highly stimulating, fast-paced, global environment we operate in, and our bold ambitions result in unique learning opportunities for our people.

job_title: Compliance, Global Privacy Office, Vice President, Birmingham
job_description:
OUR IMPACT

Our division prevents, detects and mitigates compliance, regulatory and reputational risk across the firm and helps to strengthen the firm’s culture of compliance. Compliance accomplishes these through the firm’s enterprise-wide compliance risk management program. As an independent control function and part of the firm’s second line of defense, Compliance assesses the firm’s compliance, regulatory and reputational risk; monitors for compliance with new or amended laws, rules and regulations; designs and implements controls, policies, procedures and training; conducts independent testing; investigates, surveils and monitors for compliance risks and breaches; and leads the firm’s responses to regulatory examinations, audits and inquiries. You'll be part of a team with members from a wide range of academic and professional backgrounds, such as law, accounting, sales, and trading. We look for those who possess sound judgment, curiosity, and are able to adapt to a changing regulatory landscape.

YOUR IMPACT
This is an exciting opportunity to join the Privacy Advisory team, supporting Ireland and European operations and be a member of Goldman Sachs’ Global Privacy Office (GPO). The successful candidate will work from Goldman Sachs’ Birmingham office and provide expert advice on complex privacy matters to senior stakeholders across the firm. The candidate will also play a key role in collaborating with colleagues to further build out the firm’s privacy program to address the evolving regulatory landscape, enhance divisional collaboration and increase cross-functional engagement.
Responsibilities
We are seeking a Privacy Advisory vice president with excellent analytical, communication and co-ordination skills to join the Global Privacy Office. This role will require you to develop a detailed knowledge of multiple areas within the firm and will include:
• Leading the identification and strategic assessment of privacy risks and opportunities across the firms’ business lines, products and initiatives in Ireland and the wider European marketI
• Identifying and executing opportunities to efficiently scale the firm’s global privacy program within European jurisdictions
• Providing expert privacy advisory guidance to business, engineers, operations, compliance and other stakeholders to enable the delivery and development of privacy compliant business initiatives, including the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and AI systems
• Overseeing privacy risk assessment processes (including Data Protection Impact Assessments and AI-related impact assessments) and other operational aspects of the firm’s privacy compliance program
• Reviewing and assessing products, features and business activities, including those that employ AI and AI-related technologies, against Irish and EU privacy requirements and standards
• Counselling cross-functional project teams on the privacy implications of new initiatives and regulatory change programs 
• Monitoring and reporting to senior management on the status of the privacy program
• Partnering with Legal, Compliance, Engineering, Risk and Business teams to research and assess the impact of new privacy and data protection laws or regulations (such as guidelines from the Irish Data Protection Commission and the European Data Protection Board), and managing the work to deliver required changes
• Partnering with Engineering teams to identify and design new tools, or improve existing tools, that support the firm’s privacy compliance program
• Promoting the development and implementation of privacy program governance frameworks with key stakeholders in Operations, Compliance, Technology, Legal and Risk
• Promoting a culture of privacy risk accountability across the first line of defense through engagement, education and influence
• Shaping and advising on privacy program policies and procedures, ensuring they reflect Irish regulatory expectations and business realities
• Contributing to other activities within the Global Privacy Office where necessary
Basic Qualifications
• Bachelor’s degree or international equivalent; legal degree is helpful
• CIPP/E certification is highly preferred
• At least 7 years of work experience, with at least 5 of those working in the Privacy or Data Protection domain
• Experience with reviewing, advising and/or implementing programs to address privacy laws on a local and global level (e.g., EU GDPR, Irish Data Protection Act 2018, ePrivacy Regulations, EU AI Act, etc…)
• Financial services experience is a plus, particularly within an Irish or EU-regulated entity
Required Skills
• Highly motivated with the ability to work autonomously as well as in a team and collaboration-oriented environment
• Highly organized, attention to detail and excellent follow through skills 
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; risk-based prioritization
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills to effectively articulate complex regulatory requirements to stakeholders and dependent teams at all levels of the firm
• Able to coordinate activities with multiple interdependencies and to escalate items that are unresolved or at risk
• Comfortable working with incomplete information, to ask focused questions and rapidly gain an in-depth understanding of the current processes and compare and relate to similar situations
• Detailed problem tracking, resolutions and completion of all actions and issues by their deadlines

You will develop an in-depth understanding of these entities, including their investments, business strategies, and associated technical accounting requirements. 

 We're looking for a bright, driven professional to join our Controllers team, who is keen to use and develop their technical accounting skills to provide high quality reporting and analysis of our entities' assets and liabilities in a challenging and varied environment.

 Controllers are a diverse team of specialists charged with ensuring the firm meets the financial control and reporting obligations of a global, regulated and public financial institution.

 Funding Controllers is part of the broader Controller Division which is a global team responsible for ensuring the accuracy of the firm’s financial and regulatory information by complying with the rules and regulations governing financial markets worldwide. job_description:
Global Investment Research
Global Investment Research (GIR) produces original, fundamental research and analysis of industries, companies and economies. Our research teams continually identify and analyze financial information, strategic issues and trends that affect companies, industries and markets on a regional and global scale. Our clients use these insights and investment ideas to develop their strategies. 

Our Team
The Macro Research team focuses on the intersection between economics and financial markets across a wide class of assets including equities, rates, FX, credit, mortgages and commodities. The Global Interest Rates, FX & EM Strategy team analyzes the economic and political drivers of exchange rates, local interest rates, and hard currency sovereign credit, and provides investment advice to the firm’s institutional and corporate clients.

Summary of Responsibilities
We are seeking a strategist to join the Europe Interest Rates Strategy team at the Associate level in London.

Key responsibilities include:
• Publishing timely and differentiated research on macroeconomic and political developments and their impact on interest-rate markets, as well as structural issues relevant to fixed-income strategy 
• Developing statistical and econometric models to support economic and market analysis and forecasting 
• Generating clear, actionable and implementable investment ideas 
• Presenting our market views to institutional and corporate clients and to senior stakeholders within Sales and Trading 
• Analyzing large and complex datasets and translating the findings into commercially relevant conclusions 
• Collaborating closely with the broader Macro Strategy team, regional economists and other colleagues across GIR
• Supporting internal stakeholders across the firm with timely market analysis and perspectives

Preferred Qualifications & Skillset
• Master’s degree or PhD in macroeconomics, finance, asset pricing or a closely related field
• At least three years’ experience working in macroeconomic or financial markets research, ideally with direct experience developing and communicating investment ideas
• Experience analyzing interest-rate markets and/or developed-market economies is preferred
• Strong quantitative skills and fluency in applied statistics and econometrics
• Proficiency in relevant programming languages, such as Python or R
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills
• Ability to analyze large datasets and draw clear, commercially relevant conclusions
• Deep curiosity and a strong interest in the intersection between macroeconomics and financial markets
• A collaborative and team-oriented approach
• A proactive mindset and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment and meet deadlines

About Product Management:

As a Product Manager at Grafana Labs, you'll develop a vision and strategy for your product domain. You will own your product’s roadmap, collateral, and market research, and you will collaborate with Grafana leadership on fine-tuning your product’s goals. You will be the primary advocate and expert in your area, with a strong ability to communicate needs, functionality, and details effectively both to external customers and internal stakeholders. The teams and people you will be interacting with will be 100% remote and globally distributed, so strong and proactive communication is essential.

Product Managers are the bridge that connect Engineering, Design, and UX to GTM. You are a facilitator who ensures the free flow of information across these teams and are expected to be technically proficient when representing our products to our customers. 

The opportunity:

As the Product Manager for Application Observability (App O11y), you’ll be responsible for helping application developers and SREs understand how their applications are performing, what’s affecting their users, and where to focus when something goes wrong. You’ll continue to build App O11y on top of the Knowledge Graph and fully integrate high-fidelity signals like traces and profiles, making all three first-class parts of the product experience. You’ll bring these capabilities together into our full-stack observability experience, alongside our Drilldown products, while building AI-first workflows that help customers investigate issues, understand root cause, and take action beyond static experiences. 

Your primary responsibility will be to define the vision and roadmap that takes App O11y into its next wave of adoption and revenue growth. This will require heavy customer discovery, using product data to understand where users get stuck, and working with your engineering and design partners to turn those needs into clear priorities. You’ll balance new product opportunities with the depth, performance, and reliability customers need from tracing and profiling, while working across R&D to ensure App O11y is tightly woven into our broader Grafana Cloud suite.

You’ll also work closely with PMM and GTM to help customers understand the value of App O11y. This includes shaping pricing and packaging that make it easy to get started and grow with the product. You’ll regularly review customer feedback and usage data to understand what’s working and where people get stuck, and then be accountable for turning what you learn into stronger adoption and revenue growth.

• Empathize with customer problems in order to collect user needs, requirements, and pain points

• Work closely with PMM to enable GTM on product differentiation, including creating and updating presentations, documentation, website content, datasheets, and whitepapers. 

• Use your deep product expertise to make decisions about our go-to-market strategies, pricing, packaging, licensing and tiering.

Operating at a senior leadership level, the role sets the integrated vision, strategy, and roadmap that determine how the team's combined engineering, product, and AI capabilities are prioritised, resourced, and delivered to meet CMC's clinical-to-commercial manufacturing and control needs. The role is accountable for building and developing a high-performing, cohesive team, for the quality, compliance, and value of everything the team delivers, and for representing CMC's scientific data and AI capability to senior stakeholders across R&D, Global Supply Chain, Quality, and enterprise leadership.

Responsibilities 
This role will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career. These responsibilities include some of the following: 

• Provide senior leadership and line management for the CMC Scientific Data & AI Products team, spanning forward deployment engineering, data and application product management, and agentic AI product strategy, setting a unified direction across the portfolio.
• Own overall accountability for the team's delivery, quality, and value realisation, ensuring the forward-deployed engineering, product management, and AI strategy functions operate cohesively toward shared CMC priorities.
• Set and communicate the integrated strategy and roadmap for CMC's data, application, and agentic AI product portfolio, aligning investment and resourcing decisions across disciplines with functional and enterprise priorities.
• Lead, coach, and develop direct reports and their teams, building capability, succession planning, and career pathways across engineering, product management, and AI product leadership disciplines.
• Act as the senior escalation point and decision-maker for cross-functional trade-offs, resolving competing priorities between deployment, delivery, and strategic AI initiatives.
• Represent CMC's data and AI product capability to senior stakeholders across R&D, Global Supply Chain, Quality, and enterprise leadership, securing sponsorship, resources, and alignment for the portfolio.
• Own the overall governance, data quality, and GxP compliance posture of the team's products and deployments, ensuring consistent standards are applied across all delivery streams.
• Manage the team's budget, headcount, and resourcing, including external technology partners and contractors, allocating capacity across deployment, delivery, and strategic priorities.
• Define and track portfolio-level success metrics, using these to evaluate performance, prioritise investment, and report progress to senior leadership.
• Champion responsible and compliant AI, data engineering, and product management practice across the team, fostering a culture of technical excellence, adoption, and continuous improvement.

Why You?

We are seeking professionals with the following required skills and qualifications to help us achieve our goals: 

• Bachelor's degree in computer science, Data Science, Data Engineering, Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning, Bioinformatics, Engineering, Life Sciences, or a closely related scientific or technical field.
• 12+ years of progressive experience across data engineering, AI/ML or agentic product management, and software or application delivery, including substantial experience leading and developing multidisciplinary teams (spanning engineering, product management, and AI product leadership) that deliver production-grade data and AI-enabled solutions, ideally within a pharmaceutical, CMC, or other GxP-regulated environment, with demonstrated experience managing senior/manager-level direct reports.

• Strong understanding of forward-deployed engineering, data and application product management, and agentic AI product strategy. You set direction and make sound trade-offs across all three.

• Strong track record managing budgets, headcount and resources, including external technology partners and contractors.
• Working knowledge of data governance, model validation, data quality and responsible AI practice in a regulated Good Practice (GxP) environment.
• Strong analytical skills. You define portfolio-level metrics and use evidence to guide priorities and investment.
• Experience holding senior accountability for production data and AI products, including architecture, delivery and regulatory trade-offs.
• Experience evaluating, governing and negotiating with third-party AI and data platforms, vendors and technology partners.
• Sound commercial and strategic judgement. You balance scientific value, technical feasibility, regulatory constraints and business priorities.

• Master's degree or PhD in a scientific, data science, AI/ML, or engineering discipline, or relevant senior leadership, product, or AI/cloud platform certifications

• Skilled at coaching and developing talent, building succession plans, and fostering a culture of technical excellence and continuous improvement.

The role
The Software Implementation Engineer is a hands-on technical delivery role at the centre of complex NHS deployments. At Heidi, the CSM owns the customer from day one: the relationship, the rollout plan, the path to renewal. The Implementation Engineer is the technical arm they lean on: the person who personally configures SSO with the customer's IT team, sets up and provisions tenants, delivers EHR integrations through to go-live, configures agents and custom builds, and gives every technical problem a fast diagnosis and the right owner — fixing what is configuration, and handing confirmed product defects to Support Engineering, who own and drive their resolution. 
You are the reason launches don't stall on technical topics. The remit is deliberately broad: anything to do with getting an account set up, configured and optimised is yours, from account configuration and MFA through to integration build and iteration, rather than being split across several specialist roles. 
Clinical training and adoption sit with Clinical Enablement, not here. Your ownership begins upon acceptance of the enterprise handover. It ends when the agreed technical scope has passed its acceptance criteria, customer sign-off has been recorded, the final configuration has been documented and the implementation has transferred into hypercare or BAU support. 
You are technically credible in front of a CIO, precise in what you hand to engineers, and relentless about closing the loop — and you translate what customers need technically into clear, prioritised asks for the Technical Program Manager (TPM), who owns the integration roadmap and prioritisation.
Success in this role looks like:
Hands-on delivery — you personally set up, configure and validate the technical footprint of an account: identity, provisioning, integrations, agents, data flows. Not coordinated — done.
Technical ownership — every technical problem at your accounts gets a fast diagnosis and a clear owner. What is configuration or implementation, you fix; what is a product defect, Support Engineering owns and drives — you hand it over with the diagnosis attached and do not shadow the ticket. CSMs never have to diagnose or route technical problems themselves.
Fast unblocking — technical blockers that would stall a launch for weeks get diagnosed, sequenced and resolved in days, because you understand the problem and know exactly who has to do what.
Clean boundaries — you hand net-new build work to FDEs as precise, prioritised requirements they can act on without rework, and you route live product defects to Support Engineering with a proper diagnosis attached — you don’t hoard work that belongs elsewhere, and you don’t toss problems over walls.
Trusted translation — customer IT and security teams treat you as a peer; the Technical Program Manager (TPM) gets integration gaps and technical priorities from you they can act on, and product hears a clear, prioritised signal.
This is a delivery-accountable role, so your job is to make the technical side of every account work: identity live, tenants configured, integrations delivered, agents built, security questions answered, and technical problems solved before they become escalations.
What you’ll do 
Technical Onboarding & Account Setup
Own the technical setup of new enterprise accounts end to end: tenant and workspace configuration, user provisioning and seat structure, environment readiness.
Configure SSO with the customer’s IT team — SAML / OIDC against Okta, Microsoft Entra and NHS identity infrastructure — including MFA and conditional-access alignment.
Drive network and device readiness: whitelisting, VDI and shared-device constraints, mobile device management, so clinicians can actually use Heidi on day one. Work directly with customer IT to clear whatever is blocking a swift deployment: deployment questionnaires, IT vetting, access requests, environment prerequisites.
Integration Delivery
Receive the validated integration design and signed SOW from presales. Confirm implementation prerequisites, elaborate the agreed design where necessary, configure the Heidi components, perform technical testing, support customer UAT and execute the technical go-live activities within the implementation plan you own.
Translate the agreed SOW and technical design into precise, prioritised implementation requirements; hand net-new build to FDEs in a form they can act on without rework, own the account-side delivery around it, and surface integration gaps to the Technical Program Manager. Raise any requirement that is missing, materially different or genuinely out of scope through formal change control before work proceeds, rather than absorbing scope creep silently.
Provide credible estimates, identify dependencies early and give the CSM evidence-based status and recovery options. You own the integrated technical plan, customer-facing delivery dates and dependency escalation. After go-live, keep working with the trust integration team to iterate and optimise the integration: anything that is not a product defect is yours to make work.
Product-technical Configuration
Set up agentic workflows, agents and custom builds to fit each account’s clinical and operational workflows, turning vague customer asks into scoped configurations with clear acceptance criteria.
Translate what the customer bought into what has to be configured, and set it up: products, identity, integrations, agents, APIs, exports and data flows. As Heidi adds products (agents, agentic workflows, comms), their account-level setup lands here too.
Handle technical template and coding setup where it crosses into system behaviour (clinical content stays with Clinical Enablement).
Technical Escalation & Resolution
During active implementation and hypercare, be the first technical port of call for CSMs: when something technical breaks or will not configure, you provide first-line diagnosis and make sure it lands with the right owner. Once an account has formally handed over to BAU, Support Engineering owns initial triage and ongoing incident management, and you are re-engaged only through agreed escalation criteria.
Diagnose before you route: implementation-phase and account-specific configuration issues are yours to fix; confirmed product defects go to Support Engineering with your diagnosis attached — they own and drive resolution, and Support Engineering owns defect resolution. The Implementation Engineer remains informed where the defect affects implementation milestones, acceptance criteria or customer readiness, without duplicating Support’s investigation.
Translate customer technical problems into clear priorities — routing integration gaps to the Technical Program Manager (who owns the roadmap) and confirmed defects to Support Engineering — the alignment that gets problems actually solved.
Information Governance & Security Enablement
Provide accurate technical input and evidence for DPIAs, security questionnaires and IT-assurance requests, routed through Compliance, who owns these processes. Security, Privacy and Clinical Safety retain approval authority for their respective positions. Keep them off the critical path without becoming the sign-off owner.
Work within NHS governance gates — clinical safety sign-off, IG approval, change-control windows — planning technical work around them (clinical-safety substance is owned by Heidi’s Clinical Safety Officer).
Handover acceptance and scope control
Review the signed SOW, discovery notes, technical decision record, architecture, acceptance criteria, success measures and open risk log before technical implementation begins.
Return the handover where a blocking material risk, unclear scope or unsupported commitment prevents a credible implementation plan.
Deliver against the agreed scope without converting new customer requirements into configuration work.
Classify emerging requests as in-scope configuration, defect, net-new engineering, roadmap request or commercial change.
Escalate material scope changes through the CSM, SE and AE before committing work or dates.
How we show up
Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.
Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.
Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.
Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.
Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.
Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

HPE CloudOps is seeking a high-performing, strategic Account Executive to build and grow business with leading global Cloud Service Providers (CSPs), Managed Service Providers (MSPs), telecommunications providers, and hosting partners. As a core member of the global CSP go-to-market team, you will own a named portfolio of strategic providers and lead the full relationship across executive alignment, joint business planning, service creation, commercial execution, pipeline development, launch, adoption, and expansion. This is not a traditional one-time software resale role. Success requires embedding HPE CloudOps into the provider’s service catalog, seller motion, delivery architecture, and downstream customer value proposition.

In this role, you will:
• Own a portfolio of strategic CSP and MSP accounts, including approximately 4–8 Tier 1 providers and selected Tier 2 growth accounts based on geography, market potential, executive access, and platform fit.
• Create and execute joint business plans that establish shared revenue targets, solution priorities, investment commitments, enablement requirements, routes to market, and executive governance.
• Build provider-led managed services by translating Morpheus, OpsRamp, and Zerto capabilities into packaged, priced, repeatable, and supportable service offerings.
• Generate and convert pipeline through provider sellers, co-marketing campaigns, lighthouse customers, direct customer pursuits, and expansion within the provider’s installed base.
• Lead complex commercial engagements across global and regional stakeholders while maintaining clear ownership, forecast discipline, and transparent revenue attribution.

What success looks like:
You are a builder and an executive seller. You can establish credibility with a provider’s CEO, CRO, CTO, product leaders, managed-services executives, and field sellers; create a compelling business model; and mobilize HPE’s matrixed resources to launch and scale a new service. You combine strategic thinking with operating discipline and are accountable for measurable bookings, recurring revenue, pipeline, provider activation, consumption, renewals, and multi-product attach.

Management Level Overview – Strategic Global Account Leadership
This role requires advanced expertise in complex enterprise software sales, partner business development, and cloud service provider operating models. The CSP Account Executive will manage multi-dimensional opportunities that span product strategy, service creation, architecture, commercial terms, sales enablement, customer acquisition, and long-term consumption growth.
You will operate with significant autonomy and serve as the global account leader for assigned providers. You will influence cross-functional teams across regional sales, solution engineering, product management, marketing, finance, legal, services, customer success, and executive leadership. You will also coordinate country and regional account teams to ensure that global strategy is centrally orchestrated while opportunities are locally executed and appropriately credited.

The role frequently represents HPE CloudOps with senior provider executives and industry stakeholders. It requires sound judgment, executive presence, high emotional intelligence, commercial creativity, and the ability to influence without direct authority.

Key Responsibilities – CSP Account Executive | HPE CloudOps:
As the senior account owner for a named CSP portfolio, your responsibilities will include:
• Own the end-to-end account strategy for assigned providers, including a 12–24 month growth plan, stakeholder map, whitespace analysis, competitive strategy, opportunity roadmap, and investment priorities.
• Develop and govern joint business plans with clear executive sponsors, revenue goals, service-launch milestones, enablement commitments, lighthouse targets, and quarterly business reviews.
• Lead full-cycle sales execution from proactive prospecting and value-based qualification through solution alignment, business case development, negotiation, contracting, booking, adoption, and expansion.

• Engage and influence C-level stakeholders by connecting HPE CloudOps capabilities to provider outcomes such as new recurring services revenue, operating efficiency, faster service delivery, customer retention, resilience, and margin expansion.

• Orchestrate global and regional resources across sales, presales, product, marketing, services, customer success, finance, legal, and channel teams to deliver a consistent account strategy.
• Drive provider enablement and launch readiness including seller training, technical certification, packaged demonstrations, service blueprints, pricing, support models, and field activation.
• Establish lighthouse customer wins that validate the offer, create referenceable outcomes, accelerate provider confidence, and support broader market replication.
• Maintain rigorous forecast and pipeline governance using HPE CRM and inspection processes, MEDDPICC qualification, documented next steps, risk management, and executive escalation when required.
• Track adoption, consumption, renewal, and expansion to ensure that booked business becomes durable recurring revenue and grows across the provider’s customer base.
• Represent the voice of the provider to influence product roadmap, packaging, pricing, integration priorities, support requirements, and go-to-market investments.

• 10+ years of enterprise technology sales or business-development experience, with at least 5 years selling to or through CSPs, MSPs, telecommunications providers, hosting providers, or strategic channel partners preferred.

• Proven experience creating a new business or service with a strategic partner, including joint planning, commercial modeling, enablement, launch, pipeline development, and scale.
• Established ability to engage senior executives and lead consultative, outcome-based conversations across business, product, sales, operations, and technology stakeholders.
• Experience managing long, complex sales cycles and coordinating global and regional teams across technical presales, services, customer success, finance, legal, product, and marketing.
• Working knowledge of MEDDPICC, Challenger, or a comparable enterprise sales methodology, together with strong CRM, forecasting, and inspection discipline.
• Ability and willingness to travel globally as required to support executive engagement, joint planning, launches, and strategic pursuits.
• Knowledge and Skills
• Deep understanding of CSP and MSP business models, including managed-services economics, recurring revenue, service catalogs, consumption, attach, channels, and downstream customer acquisition.
• Strong knowledge of hybrid cloud operations, cloud management, observability, AIOps, automation, FinOps, data protection, disaster recovery, cyber resilience, and IT service management.
• Ability to position the HPE CloudOps portfolio as one integrated platform strategy, while understanding where Morpheus, OpsRamp, and Zerto create distinct and combined provider value.
• Expertise in strategic account planning and executive selling, including stakeholder mapping, value articulation, commercial negotiation, governance, and multi-year relationship development.
• Proven partner and ecosystem leadership, with the ability to align provider executives, provider sellers, HPE account teams, distributors, GSIs, ISVs, and technology alliances around shared outcomes.

Job Description
Network for AI - Inside Solutions Architect / Specialist 

About the Role
The Network for AI (NFAI) Inside Solutions Architect / Specialist is responsible for driving data center networking and routing solution opportunities across commercial and lower-tier enterprise accounts through a virtual-first engagement model.

This role serves as the inside counterpart to field-led enterprise specialist coverage, owning a defined segment of accounts where opportunities may involve meaningful technical complexity, multi-stakeholder buying processes, and executive alignment. In addition to sales responsibilities, the role acts as a subject matter expert (SME) for the NFAI portfolio, providing solution design guidance and architectural perspective to Account Managers and Sales Engineers.

Success in this role requires a seller who can balance the efficiency of an inside model with the technical depth required to design credible architectures, guide solution direction, and support account teams in positioning HPE Networking technologies effectively. The role frequently partners with Account Managers, Sales Engineers, partners, and field specialists to develop pipeline, shape opportunities, and deliver technically sound networking solutions.

Bi-lingual English / French or, English / German language skills are highly preferable.

Key Responsibilities
Sales Execution & Opportunity Development
• Drive pipeline development and revenue growth for HPE Networking’s data center networking, routing, and AI infrastructure connectivity portfolio across assigned commercial and lower-tier enterprise accounts.
• Lead consultative discovery conversations to understand customer business objectives, infrastructure requirements, and modernization initiatives.
• Translate business and technical requirements into solution architectures in collaboration with Sales Engineers, recommending appropriate designs, deployment models, and phased adoption strategies.
• Provide architectural guidance during early opportunity stages, helping customers and internal teams evaluate topology options, fabric architectures, scalability considerations, and integration points.
• Progress opportunities using structured sales methodologies (such as MEDDPICC), ensuring alignment around decision criteria, business value, and stakeholder sponsorship.
• Build and communicate compelling business cases that connect networking modernization initiatives to measurable business outcomes such as scalability, performance, resilience, operational efficiency, and cost optimization.

Customer & Executive Engagement
• Establish trusted relationships with technical and business stakeholders including network architects, IT managers, infrastructure leaders, and operations teams.
• Engage confidently with director-, VP-, and selected C-level stakeholders when executive sponsorship is required to advance an opportunity.
• Navigate complex buying committees and align internal and external stakeholders around architecture direction and investment rationale.

Technical Leadership & SME Support
• Act as a subject matter expert for the NFAI portfolio, supporting Account Managers and Sales Engineers with technical positioning, solution architecture guidance, and competitive differentiation.
• Assist account teams in designing networking solutions that align with validated architectures, customer requirements, and HPE Networking best practices.
• Provide architectural input during account strategy development, helping teams identify modernization opportunities and expansion paths.
• Support technical discussions such as solution topology, scalability planning, integration with compute/storage platforms, and AI infrastructure connectivity requirements.
• Collaborate with Sales Engineers on detailed solution validation while maintaining ownership of overall solution strategy and value articulation.

Partner & Internal Collaboration
• Collaborate closely with Account Managers, Sales Engineers, channel partners, and field specialists to advance complex opportunities and ensure coordinated pursuit strategies.
• Qualify when to lead independently versus when to engage additional technical, executive, or specialist resources based on opportunity complexity and account dynamics.
• Leverage partner ecosystems to expand reach, accelerate solution adoption, and support joint account strategies.

Pipeline & Forecast Discipline
• Maintain accurate pipeline visibility, forecasting, and opportunity hygiene within Salesforce and associated sales tools.
• Apply disciplined opportunity qualification and prioritization to ensure efficient use of time and resources across a higher-volume inside sales environment.

Portfolio & Market Expertise
• Maintain deep working knowledge of HPE Networking’s data center switching, routing, AI networking, and fabric architectures.
• Understand how networking infrastructure integrates with compute, storage, and AI workloads within modern data center and hybrid cloud environments.
• Stay current on validated designs, architectural best practices, and evolving networking technologies relevant to AI and data center modernization.
• Maintain awareness of competitive networking technologies to articulate architectural differentiation and displacement strategies.

Scope & Complexity
• Owns a defined set of commercial and lower-tier enterprise accounts, typically domestic or regional in scope.
• Opportunities may range from incremental infrastructure expansion to competitive replacements and architectural modernization initiatives.
• Handles a higher volume of opportunities than field-led specialist roles while still navigating meaningful technical complexity and multi-stakeholder buying environments.
• Frequently supports account teams as an architectural SME while advancing sales pursuits through an inside engagement model.

Education & Experience
• 6–8+ years of experience in networking technology sales, specialist sales, or hybrid technical-commercial roles.
• Proven success selling and positioning networking infrastructure solutions within commercial and/or enterprise environments.
• Demonstrated ability to participate in or lead solution architecture discussions related to switching, routing, and data center networking.
• Experience collaborating with Sales Engineers on solution design and technical validation.
• Candidates with slightly less experience must demonstrate exceptional technical credibility, executive communication skills, and a track record of supporting complex infrastructure solutions.

Knowledge & Skills
• Strong understanding of data center networking architectures including leaf-spine designs, fabric architectures, and scalable routing solutions.
• Ability to translate customer requirements into credible solution designs and architectural approaches.
• Capability to provide SME support to account teams by guiding solution positioning, architecture decisions, and technical strategy.
• Strong executive communication skills and ability to build credibility with both technical and business stakeholders.
• High level of sales discipline, forecasting accuracy, and opportunity management rigor.
• Ability to thrive in a fast-paced inside sales environment that requires balancing technical engagement with opportunity volume.

Responsible for owning and leading the HPE Alletra Storage MP X10000 business in-GEO. Sales-led and accountable for the planning, the sales funnel and making Data Solutions the platform of choice inside HPC & AI.

The Lead Storage Sales Specialist is the primary Subject Matter Expert for Storage and related products. Responsible for driving storage sales in an assigned territory, industry, or account(s). Demonstrates solid understanding of the features and benefits in the area of evolving storage technical solutions as well as how HPE solutions are differentiated from the competition. Maintains an outside-in view, stays abreast of competitors, leverages HPE’s opportunities and mitigates challenges. 

Exercises deep expertise of end to end data solutions leveraging the HPE storage portfolio and ecosystem of partners. Effectively uses references to craft a story that makes complex technologies seem simple & understandable for our customers. 

Actively hunts for solution opportunities in acquisition and development accounts to pursue new business. Actively generates customer interest and links business & financial benefits with technology. Brings a services-led approach to build stickiness through consultative engagements and financial constructs. Laser focused on the channel to forge relationships, provide enablement of key technologies, and co-sell to end-users. 

Key Responsibilities:

• Own the GEO X10000 business: Write and run the 12–18 month plan. Be the single point of accountability for bookings, pipeline quality, forecast and competitive position across the GEO, with a hard focus on UK, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.
• Build and convert the funnel: Originate and co-originate opportunities. Qualify hard. Lead major pursuits. Maintain a living account and opportunity map so the next several quarters of revenue are visible, not hoped for.
• Make Data Solutions default inside HPC & AI: Build a working alliance with the GEO HPC / AI organisation. Ensure material AI Factory, Private Cloud AI, sovereign AI and HPC pursuits have an explicit data-platform decision — with X10000 as the primary platform of choice, not an optional attach.
• Open new personas and ship sales plays: Engage data-layer and AI buyers (CDO, CAIO, Head of HPC, data-platform, cyber-recovery), not only storage. Build practical plays that take the field from current knowledge to the required state: AI data layer, sovereign AI, data lakes / RAG, modern protection, competitive take-out.
• Enable the wider GEO Data Solutions team: Lift sales and presales competency and confidence so X10000 is sold without this person in every meeting. Coach live deals. Create named seller + SE champions in each priority country.
• Drive ISV, partner and GSI engagement: Prioritise a short list and run named joint pursuits — NVIDIA ecosystem, selected ISVs, GSIs and local GCC partners. Partners must change architectures and source pipeline, not decorate slides.

Attributes:

• Owner, not commentator: Has carried a number — quota, pipeline, forecast — and built a multi-country or GEO motion, not only run inbound deals in one market.
• Credible in the theatre: Depth in at least two of unstructured / object / parallel file, HPC, enterprise AI infrastructure, or data platforms. Can brief a Head of AI or HPC without sliding into array feature-speak.
• Multiplier through the line: Sells with lined account teams and partners, not around them. Builds plays people actually use. Measures enablement by other people’s pipeline.
• Commercially and politically adult: Fluent in a matrix. Sharp on deal desk, consumption / GreenLake and close plans. Honest on competition in Data Solutions & Storage.
• Travel: Willingness to travel the UK–KSA–UAE triangle. High agency in programmes that move slowly, then all at once. Fluency in English both written and verbally is required. Fluency in Arabic would be a real advantage but not essential.

Education and Experience:

• University or Bachelor's degree; Advanced Degree or MBA preferred.
• Demonstrated achievement of progressively higher quota, interface with diverse business customers at all levels.
• Typically, 8 + years of sales experience.
• Extensive experience in Unstructured Data Solutions storage sales, typically 3-5+ years.
• Prior selling experience includes multiple, diverse set of selling responsibilities.
• Project management experience required.

Storage Specialist- Sales Acumen & Behaviours:
• Possesses expertise to be able to assess solution feasibility from a technical and business perspective, to determine "qualify-in"/"qualify-out" status.
• Uses expertise to negotiate and drive deals to ensure successful closure and a high win rate.
• Demonstrates hunter mentality to actively pursue solution opportunities in acquisition and development accounts and to pursue new business.
• Possesses the ability to independently articulate the technical solution and the commercial benefits to the client.
• Possesses knowledge of digital and modern methods to connect and sell.
• Uses storage knowledge to actively prospects within accounts to discover or cultivate sales opportunities.

Technology Focus:
• Is considered a master in knowledge of storage, cloud, solution and/or service offerings as well as competitor's offerings to be able to sell large, complex solutions.
• Understands the outside-in view and possesses deep knowledge of industry trends. Stays abreast of competitors and key partner/ISV solutions, including both traditional and emerging vendors. Leverages HPE's opportunities and mitigates any challenges. Member of an industry organization and/or professional network relative to a trend or vertical. • Know strengths and weaknesses of key competitors in the account. Understands how to leverage this knowledge in the account and integrates this knowledge into consultative selling.

• Possesses deep expertise of end to end data solutions leveraging the HPE storage portfolio and ecosystem of partners, with a strong focus on traditional and modern applications. Able to change the playing field on our competitors.
• Uses C-level engagement skills in collaboration with account leads to offer value-add solutions to the client.
