To provide senior leadership and end-to-end accountability for CMC's scientific data, application, and AI product portfolio, leading a multidisciplinary team spanning forward-deployed engineering, data and application product management, and agentic AI product strategy. Operating at a senior leadership level, the role sets the integrated vision, strategy, and roadmap that determine how the team's combined engineering, product, and AI capabilities are prioritised, resourced, and delivered to meet CMC's clinical-to-commercial manufacturing and control needs. The role is accountable for building and developing a high-performing, cohesive team, for the quality, compliance, and value of everything the team delivers, and for representing CMC's scientific data and AI capability to senior stakeholders across R&D, Global Supply Chain, Quality, and enterprise leadership.

Responsibilities 
This role will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career. These responsibilities include some of the following: 

• Provide senior leadership and line management for the CMC Scientific Data & AI Products team, spanning forward deployment engineering, data and application product management, and agentic AI product strategy, setting a unified direction across the portfolio.
• Own overall accountability for the team's delivery, quality, and value realisation, ensuring the forward-deployed engineering, product management, and AI strategy functions operate cohesively toward shared CMC priorities.
• Set and communicate the integrated strategy and roadmap for CMC's data, application, and agentic AI product portfolio, aligning investment and resourcing decisions across disciplines with functional and enterprise priorities.
• Lead, coach, and develop direct reports and their teams, building capability, succession planning, and career pathways across engineering, product management, and AI product leadership disciplines.
• Act as the senior escalation point and decision-maker for cross-functional trade-offs, resolving competing priorities between deployment, delivery, and strategic AI initiatives.
• Represent CMC's data and AI product capability to senior stakeholders across R&D, Global Supply Chain, Quality, and enterprise leadership, securing sponsorship, resources, and alignment for the portfolio.
• Own the overall governance, data quality, and GxP compliance posture of the team's products and deployments, ensuring consistent standards are applied across all delivery streams.
• Manage the team's budget, headcount, and resourcing, including external technology partners and contractors, allocating capacity across deployment, delivery, and strategic priorities.
• Define and track portfolio-level success metrics, using these to evaluate performance, prioritise investment, and report progress to senior leadership.

Role Purpose

The Strategic Data & Analytics team builds the analytical products that support growth across Howden Employee Benefits. We are a business-embedded team that works directly alongside consultants, client directors and project teams, rather than operating within a traditional technology or IT function. Our products are used every day by colleagues across the UK business and by our clients to support better decision-making, solve complex challenges and deliver stronger outcomes.

This role builds those products. You will own delivery end to end, and lead the reusable components, frameworks, templates and working practices that allow a small team to serve the whole business. Our approach is simple: build fewer things, build them fast, and build them once so they can be used many times.

This is not a software engineering role and it is not an IT role. We are a consulting team that is proficient with technology. You will spend as much time working out what a senior leader actually needs to decide as writing the code that answers it.

Location is flexible, with home-based or local Howden office-based both available according to preference. The team itself is distributed across home and several Howden offices and works together primarily over Teams rather than in one room. Our closeness to the business is organisational rather than geographic.

Key Accountabilities

Work directly with senior leaders and client-facing colleagues to turn a broad commercial question into a defined, decidable one, and to turn the answer into a product rather than a one-off analysis.
Own delivery of analytical products end to end, from first conversations through to something in production that real users depend on.
Lead the development of the reusable components, libraries, frameworks, templates and working practices the rest of the team builds on.
Build for reuse and hand-off: configurable, documented and maintainable by someone other than you.
Work within the firm’s software development lifecycle and governance requirements, and help shape them where they do not yet fit how a small product team works.
Support the technical development of colleagues, including reviewing their work. This is not a line management role.
Keep delivery momentum when priorities move, which they will.

Skills & Experience

The first question is whether this is the right environment for you.

You have a consulting mindset and enjoy working across a wide variety of problems.
You enjoy helping senior leaders and their teams make better decisions, and you see data, analytics and visualisation as your tools for bringing that about.
You can explain technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
You support the people around you, in the small everyday moments and the bigger challenges. You share what you learn, you would rather have an honest conversation than a comfortableone, and you build your own network across the business. In a small team we succeed together, and nothing we build succeeds unless the business succeeds with it.
You take ownership of your decisions, your actions and your outputs.
You are comfortable with uncertainty and speed, and are interested rather than frustrated by new problems with incomplete and ambiguous information.
You can work in a fast-growing firm where processes, systems and structures are still being brought together, and where parts of the environment are incomplete.
You are effective in a distributed team. Most of our collaboration, with each other and with the business, happens over Teams, with colleagues you will meet in person occasionally rather than daily. If you do your best work by turning to the person beside you, this will be a difficult environment.

You have taken more than one analytical product from an incomplete brief through to sustained use by people who did not commission it. Delivery matters to us more than cleverness.
You have built the reusable parts that colleagues then worked from, and you have lived with what you built after release: supported it, changed it under pressure, and let that change how you build next time. This would not be your first role building analytical products.
You have substantial experience building analytical products in Python. Experience of Employee Benefits, Pensions or Insurance is not required.

Our successes have all come from someone brave enough to try something new

Job Description: 
Let's Shape Tomorrow's Cybersecurity Ecosystem

At Ingram Micro, we're helping businesses realize the promise of technology. As one of the world's leading technology distributors and solutions aggregators, we connect manufacturers, resellers, and customers with the innovations they need to grow, compete, and transform. Every day, we help organizations navigate an increasingly complex technology landscape, creating opportunities that shape the future of business.

Our Cyber business plays a critical role in that mission. As cybersecurity continues to be a top priority for organizations worldwide, our team identifies, enables, and scales innovative security vendors across the region. By combining deep market expertise, strong partner relationships, and global reach, we help bring cutting-edge cybersecurity solutions to customers throughout EMEA.

At Ingram Micro, how we achieve results matters as much as the outcomes themselves. We foster a culture built on Results, Integrity, Imagination, Courage, Responsibility, and Talent. We collaborate across borders, challenge conventional thinking, act with accountability, and invest in one another's success. Together, we create an environment where diverse perspectives are valued and innovation thrives.

About the Role
As Cyber Distribution Vendor Manager, EMEA, you will lead the identification, recruitment, onboarding, and growth of strategic cybersecurity vendors across the region. Acting as the primary link between vendor partners and country organizations, you will help expand our cybersecurity portfolio, accelerate go-to-market execution, and drive successful vendor adoption across multiple markets.

This is a highly visible role combining business development, relationship management, strategic planning, and cross-functional leadership. You will work closely with vendors, country sales leaders, marketing, technical teams, and executive stakeholders to maximize growth opportunities and strengthen Ingram Micro's position within the cybersecurity ecosystem.

What You'll Do
Identify, assess, and recruit strategic cybersecurity vendors aligned with Ingram Micro's EMEA growth strategy.
Build and maintain a robust pipeline of vendor opportunities across key cybersecurity segments.
Lead vendor engagement from initial discussions through commercial negotiations and contract execution.
Develop compelling business cases and present Ingram Micro's value proposition, market reach, and route-to-market capabilities.
Drive regional onboarding and launch plans, ensuring readiness across sales, technical, marketing, and operational teams.
Partner with country organizations to develop local go-to-market strategies and accelerate vendor adoption.
Build trusted executive-level relationships with vendor stakeholders and serve as their primary EMEA point of contact.
Monitor business performance, facilitate strategic business reviews, and identify opportunities to drive mutual growth.

What You'll Bring
Proven experience in cybersecurity, technology distribution, channel development, vendor management, or partner ecosystems.
Strong knowledge of the cybersecurity landscape, vendor marketplace, and channel dynamics.
Demonstrated success recruiting, onboarding, and developing strategic vendor partnerships.
Experience leading complex commercial discussions, RFIs, due diligence initiatives, and contract negotiations.
Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence senior leaders internally and externally.
Commercially minded with excellent negotiation, relationship-building, and business planning capabilities.
Strong project management skills with the ability to coordinate multiple priorities across countries and functions.
Experience working within a multicultural EMEA environment and collaborating across diverse teams and markets.

Why Join Ingram Micro?
This is more than a vendor management role. It's an opportunity to influence the future of cybersecurity across one of the world's most dynamic technology ecosystems. You'll collaborate with industry-leading vendors, work on strategic growth initiatives, and help bring innovative solutions to market at scale.
At Ingram Micro, you'll find the support, development opportunities, global exposure, and inclusive culture needed to build a successful long-term career. If you're energized by creating partnerships, driving growth, and shaping the future of cybersecurity, we'd love to hear from you.

Let's shape tomorrow together.

Here, your CRM ideas go from first test to real results, and you’ll see the difference they make.

 

$113M funded. Global footprint. AI-powered. Human-driven. 🚀

INSHUR is the embedded insurance powerhouse for the on-demand world. We partner with giants like Uber and Amazon to provide fair, data-backed coverage for the modern workforce. We’re 200 people strong across the UK, US, and Netherlands, using AI as a multiplier to stay ahead of the curve. Want to work where tech actually meets the road? You’re in the right place.

Find out more about our history, values, hiring process and more here https://inshur.slab.com/public/topics/inshur-playbook-dr5k6re7.

 
 


THE ROLE

You’ll own our marketing CRM across the UK, US and Netherlands, creating the in-life communications, automations and campaigns that help customers choose us and stay with us. You’ll have real autonomy to test, learn and experiment, turning data into ideas and ideas into results. With a colleague looking after HubSpot’s sales, operational and data foundations, you’re free to focus on building multi-channel campaigns, shaping the CRM roadmap and making every customer touchpoint count. You’ll be the CRM expert in a growing marketing team, partnering with UK and US generalists and paid media specialists.

In your first year, success looks like stronger renewals, growing quote-to-policy conversion, and less manual effort in getting campaigns live.

This role reports to the Head of Marketing and sits within a growing team of 3.

We’re based in Brighton, with a hybrid working model. You’ll come into the office 1 day a week, with the rest of your time remote.

 
 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Owning in-life communications: Building and continually improving the journeys that matter most, from quote follow-ups to renewal invites, so every message lands at the right moment.

 - Building a data-led campaign roadmap: Planning and delivering targeted CRM communications, then learning from every result to make the next campaign even better.

 - Bringing campaigns to life end to end: Owning the content calendar and creating campaigns from first idea to final send, including the copy, the build and the testing.

 - Growing customer lifetime value: Designing segmented retention, win-back and loyalty campaigns, and spotting the right moments for upsell and cross-sell.

 - Testing and learning with purpose: Framing each experiment as a simple one-page business case, measuring what happens, and sharing insights that help the whole business make better decisions.

 - Listening to our customers: Looking after customer sentiment, including NPS, feedback surveys and Trustpilot, and sharing what you find with stakeholders as part of our Consumer Duty work.

 - Powering wider marketing and partners: Creating segments for paid media, such as exclusion and lookalike audiences, and supporting new product and partner launches with seamless CRM journeys.

 
 


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

We care more about how you think than what’s on your CV. If you meet most of the essentials and are excited about the problem, apply.


ESSENTIAL

 - Solid, hands-on CRM experience: You’ve built and run multi-channel lifecycle campaigns and automations yourself, ideally in HubSpot, rather than only sending emails from a platform someone else set up.

 - Data-led, commercial thinking: You enjoy finding the story in the data, running a campaign to improve a metric, and learning from the results.

 - Self-sufficient creativity: You’re happy writing your own content and building your own emails, rolling up your sleeves to get great work out the door.

 - GDPR and marketing permissions knowledge: You understand the rules that keep customer communications compliant, so we can engage with confidence and care.

 - Curiosity and the confidence to challenge: You ask why things are done a certain way, suggest better ones, and welcome open, direct feedback that helps the work improve.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Insurance or regulated industry experience: Helpful for getting up to speed quickly, though we’re open to people from any industry, B2B or B2C.

 - A marketing or related qualification: A useful grounding, though experience matters just as much.

 
 


HOW THE MARKETING TEAM USES AI

Whether you’re new to AI or already building with it, we give everyone the tools, time, and support to grow. AI is a multiplier here, it handles the repetitive so you can focus on the work that actually needs you.

Across marketing, this involves leveraging smart tools to streamline copywriting, automations, and template creation, while ensuring every output stays human-led through thorough review and testing

We also use AI tools to support our hiring process — not to make decisions, but to help us run a fairer, faster process. You can read more about how we approach that here https://inshur.slab.com/public/posts/%F0%9F%A4%96-how-to-collaborate-with-ai-during-our-hiring-process-g625ns7t, including tips for how you can use AI to prepare.

 
 


WHAT TO EXPECT FROM THE PROCESS

 - Screen: A 30-minute call with the Talent team. We’ll cover the role, your background, and your questions.

 - First interview: 60-minute call with our Head of Marketing and People Team to delve deeper into your experience and team fit

 - Campaign walkthrough: Onsite 60 minute interview where you walk us through a recent complex campaign you’ve run, using a few slides or visuals

We design this to be a two-way conversation. Come with questions — we want you to leave knowing whether this is the right move for you.

 
 


WHAT WE OFFER

We’ve also built a benefits package that invests in our people’s long-term personal and professional growth and wellbeing. Here’s a sample of what this includes;

 - Salary £40,000 to £50,000, depending on experience plus stock options for every employee

 - 30 days of holiday annually, plus bank holidays

 - Private healthcare for you and your family, including pre-existing conditions

 - Life insurance at 3x your salary

 - 13 weeks parental leave at full pay for new parents

 - Workplace nursery scheme with Gogeta, allowing you to pay fees pre-tax

 - Ride to work scheme

 - Workplace pension scheme to help you save for retirement

 - Flexible working hours to suit your lifestyle

 - £500 annual personal training allowance plus regular learning opportunities on a variety of topics

 - £40 monthly wellbeing to keep you healthy

 - 24/7 Employee Assistance Program, covering you and immediate family members—offering crisis support, counselling, legal advice, menopause CBT, and more

 - Unlimited AI usage

 
 


WORKING HERE

You’ll do well here if you:
 🚀 Move through ambiguity without waiting for a perfect brief
 👊 Take ownership of outcomes, not just tasks
 ⚡ Adapt quickly when priorities shift, and help others do the same
 🔧 Look for ways to improve how things work, not just how to complete them
 🧠 Use tools, data, and colleagues to make better decisions

This probably isn’t the right fit if you:
 📋 Prefer clearly defined processes and a stable, slow-moving environment
 🚧 Are most comfortable staying within the boundaries of your job description
 🔄 Find frequent context-switching draining rather than energising

 
 


INCLUSION AND FLEXIBILITY

INSHUR is committed to building a team where everyone can bring their full self to work. We follow a structured hiring process and train our interview teams to support fairness and reduce bias.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, colour, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or age.

This role is advertised as full-time. We’re open to discussing part-time, job-sharing, or other flexible arrangements for the right person.

If you need any adjustments during the process, let us know and we’ll do our best to accommodate.

• Understanding of customer data, APIs, integrations and supporting digital services.

Job Summary
Insulet is seeking an experienced SAP Business Solution Architect to lead the design and evolution of end-to-end SAP solutions, with primary emphasis on commercial and customer-facing capabilities. The role will provide architecture leadership across Contract to Cash, Record to Report, Source to Pay and Inventory to Deliver, working closely with SAP functional teams and business stakeholders to create integrated, scalable and compliant solutions.

The successful candidate will combine strong business process knowledge with excellent solution and technical architecture capability. They will connect SAP functional design with MuleSoft integration, enterprise data architecture, SAP Business Technology Platform and responsible AI enablement. They will act as a trusted adviser who can respectfully challenge predetermined solutions and influence decisions towards simpler, reusable and sustainable outcomes.

Key Accountabilities
1. End-to-End Solution Architecture
• Own the end-to-end solution architecture for initiatives spanning SAP and connected enterprise platforms.
• Translate business strategy, capabilities and requirements into coherent target-state solution designs and roadmaps.
• Ensure functional, application, integration, data, security, infrastructure and support considerations are addressed as one design.
• Assess solution options and trade-offs, including business value, regulatory risk, total cost of ownership, scalability and technical debt.

2. SAP Functional Landscape Leadership
• Partner with SAP functional leads to establish consistent cross-process designs and prevent siloed decisions.
• Provide architecture oversight across Contract to Cash / Order to Cash, including contract management, customer master, pricing, order management, fulfilment, billing, accounts receivable and customer service integration.
• Provide architecture oversight across Record to Report / Finance, Source to Pay and Inventory to Deliver.
• Ensure dependencies across commercial, finance, procurement, supply chain, quality and manufacturing domains are understood and managed.

3. MuleSoft & Enterprise Integration Architecture
• Define and govern integration architecture between SAP and platforms such as Salesforce, manufacturing, quality, data, partner and regulatory solutions.
• Promote API-led, reusable and appropriately event-driven integration patterns using MuleSoft.
• Establish principles for system, process and experience APIs, interface ownership, canonical data, versioning and lifecycle management.
• Ensure designs address security, observability, error handling, retry, idempotency, sequencing, performance and recoverability.

4. Data Architecture & Governance
• Define data architecture for contract, customer, product, pricing, supplier, inventory, order and finance domains.
• Clarify systems of record, data ownership, stewardship, quality rules, lineage, retention and reconciliation requirements.
• Partner with enterprise data teams to enable trusted reporting, analytics and AI use cases.

5. SAP BTP & AI Architecture
• Shape the appropriate use of SAP Business Technology Platform for SAP extensions, integration, automation, data and AI services.
• Evaluate SAP Integration Suite, SAP Build, SAP Datasphere / Business Data Cloud and SAP AI capabilities where aligned to enterprise strategy.
• Define guardrails for clean-core extensibility, side-by-side applications, reusable services and lifecycle management.
• Ensure AI solutions follow responsible AI, cybersecurity, privacy, data quality, validation and human oversight principles.

6. Architecture Principles & Governance
• Develop architectural principles, standards, patterns, decision records and reference architectures for the SAP landscape.
• Champion clean core, standardisation, simplification, composability, reuse and fit-for-purpose design.
• Lead or contribute to architecture review boards, design authorities and solution assurance activities.

7. Business Partnership & Influence
• Build trusted relationships with senior business stakeholders, product owners, process owners and technology leaders.
• Challenge predetermined solutions constructively, reframing discussions around outcomes, evidence, risk and enterprise value.
• Communicate complex concepts clearly and influence without direct authority.

8. Regulated Environment, Quality & Controls
• Ensure solution designs support applicable GxP, SOX, privacy, cybersecurity and medical device quality requirements.
• Apply risk-based thinking to validated systems, electronic records, audit trails, access controls and data integrity.
• Partner with Quality, Compliance, Security and Internal Controls teams to embed compliance by design.

Experience & Qualifications

• Significant SAP experience in complex global organisations, including solution or enterprise architecture roles.
• Strong knowledge of SAP S/4HANA and end-to-end processes across CTC/OTC, R2R/Finance, STP and ITD.
• Strong MuleSoft and API architecture knowledge.
• Strong understanding of enterprise data architecture, master data and data governance.
• Good knowledge of SAP BTP architecture, extensibility and platform governance.
• Excellent business process analysis, communication, facilitation and stakeholder influencing skills.
Desirable
• Experience in medical device, life sciences, pharmaceutical or similarly regulated environments.
• Knowledge of GxP, computer system validation, SOX controls and data integrity.
• Experience with Salesforce integrations and customer-facing platforms.
• Knowledge of SAP Integration Suite, SAP Build, SAP Datasphere, Business Data Cloud, Signavio or LeanIX.
• Understanding of SAP AI, Joule, generative AI patterns and responsible AI governance.
• TOGAF, SAP, MuleSoft or related architecture certification.
Measures of Success
• Stakeholders have a clear, agreed target architecture and decision path.
• Solutions demonstrate stronger end-to-end process coherence, reuse and simplification.
• Integration and data designs are resilient, governed and supportable.
• Architecture risks, exceptions and technical debt are visible and actively managed.
• BTP, automation and AI are adopted selectively against credible value and compliance criteria.

Job Summary
As a vital member of the International Insights & Analytics team, the Senior Manager, International Market Insights will lead the generation and application of customer, market and competitive insights to support rigorous, fact-based strategic and commercial decisions across the International business.

The role is intentionally weighted towards primary market research and customer journey work, which will represent approximately two-thirds of the position. The remaining one-third will focus on developing, maintaining and improving International market models. The individual will integrate qualitative and quantitative research, customer and patient journey insights, internal and external data, and market analytics into clear implications and actionable recommendations.

The successful candidate will work collaboratively across Regions and Functions to build high-quality research, customer journey and market modelling capabilities, and to ensure insights are translated into strategies, priorities and commercial actions. The role requires a detail-oriented, self-motivated leader with strong analytical, problem-solving, project management and communication skills.

Key Responsibilities

Primary Market Research and Customer Journey (approximately 2/3)

• Lead end-to-end qualitative and quantitative primary market research across International markets, from business question definition and research design through fieldwork, analysis, synthesis and recommendation development.
• Advise stakeholders on fit-for-purpose research methodologies, sampling approaches and study designs, ensuring work is rigorous, efficient and aligned to the decision required.
• Translate diverse customer, patient, healthcare professional and market inputs into clear insights, implications and actionable recommendations for commercial teams and senior leaders.
• Oversee and continuously improve primary market research methodologies, standards, capabilities, governance and process efficiencies across the International organisation.
• Develop and maintain customer and patient journey frameworks, including market landscapes, buying processes, customer mapping, ecosystem mapping and key moments that influence adoption, initiation and ongoing experience.
• Create and evolve detailed customer journey maps that support go-to-market strategies for product launches, lifecycle initiatives and partnerships, reflecting customer needs at each interaction.
• Partner with regional, country, franchise and cross-functional teams to translate business and brand strategies into actionable customer journey priorities and commercial interventions.
• Document journey evolution and future-state designs as strategies, evidence and customer feedback change, ensuring alignment across functions and markets.
• Collaborate cross-functionally to guide commercial workstreams and ensure insights are embedded in strategies, tactics, launch planning and prioritisation decisions.
• Manage research agency and vendor relationships, including scoping, selection, contracts, quality, timelines and budgets, as required.

International Market Model Development (approximately 1/3)

• Lead the ongoing development, maintenance and improvement of International market models, working with regional, country and functional stakeholders to establish clear assumptions, inputs, definitions and outputs.
• Integrate internal and external data to size markets, understand market dynamics, evaluate growth opportunities and support strategic planning across geographies, channels, technologies and customer segments.
• Enhance market analytics and forecasting inputs used in annual and long-range planning, product and portfolio assessments, launch planning and commercial prioritisation.
• Conduct scenario and sensitivity analyses to test assumptions, identify key value drivers and clarify potential business implications.
• Establish consistent market model processes, documentation, quality checks and reporting outputs to improve transparency, comparability and repeatability across International markets.
• Monitor macroeconomic, healthcare, competitive and environmental trends, identifying potential implications for market development and commercial strategy.

Required Skills and Competencies

• Seasoned expertise in managing qualitative and quantitative primary market research, including methodology selection, research design, agency management, insight synthesis and recommendation development.

About the position

We're opening our first internships in the Formal Methods group of our OCaml Language team, which develops language features and tooling for correctness reasoning and bug finding in OCaml programs. With the emergence of agentic programming, we think formal methods will play a major role in helping validate agent-generated code and providing feedback for agents. Our vision is to make formal methods as useful a tool for building software as type systems are for us today, both by leveraging existing tools and technology, and pursuing novel approaches. 

During the internship, we want to give you a real sense of what it's like to work at Jane Street full time while also providing a truly unparalleled educational experience. You'll be paired with full-time employees who act as mentors, collaborating with you on a real-world project that combines your research background with one of our active projects, such as adding support for property-based testing of formal specifications or developing a refinement type system for functional correctness verification. You’ll have the opportunity to evaluate the tools you develop on a large, actively developed production codebase. You'll also be able to attend guest speakers and social events, and hopefully get a real sense of what it would be like to work here full-time.

There is plenty of work on combining agents and formal methods. What’s different at Jane Street is that we aren't stuck designing verification tools for legacy languages: we can modify and improve OxCaml, our branch of OCaml, and its development environment to make them well-suited for proof-driven software development. Moreover, we have a community of excellent programmers who are eager to adopt these tools and apply them to real software.

The role:

As a Programme Manager within the Product Solutions team, you will help deliver new partner, product and market launches. You will manage complex, cross functional programmes from initial scoping through launch and ramp up, ensuring a smooth handover to the Partner Manager.

This is a global role, initially focused on new partner launches using existing technology in markets where we already operate. You'll typically manage two to three programmes at a time, with partner onboarding taking around two to six months. Within your first six months, you'll be owning new partner onboardings end to end.

You'll work across Product, Technology, Risk, Legal, Collections, Marketing and Commercial, as well as directly with partners. Your job isn't to do every team's work: it's to make the plan clear, agree responsibilities, surface risks early and keep delivery moving.

 

What you'll get to do:

• Work day-to-day with partner stakeholders, running working groups, managing expectations and resolving blockers. Turn partner requirements into clear asks for Product and Engineering, keeping both sides aligned to the agreed scope.

• Keep stakeholders informed with proactive updates on progress, risks, decisions and changes to the plan.

• Hold teams to agreed commitments, have constructive conversations when work is delayed and use the right escalation routes to unblock delivery.

• Recommend how to respond when priorities change or a partner is delayed, helping relationship owners and roadmap owners make informed decisions.

• Confirm launch readiness, monitor early performance and coordinate fixes to launch issues. Hand over the ongoing partner relationship and growth to the Partner Manager, with clear ownership of outstanding actions.

About the Role
Payroll across 14 countries currently operates through five delivery models: Deel (standard and EOR), Arpi in Poland, ADP as a PEO in the US, and an in-house payroll in Tunisia. The process depends on a small number of named individuals, with limited documented processes and trained backup.
We're looking for a Payroll Specialist – Project Lead to address this and establish a sustainable global payroll operating model.
This is a build role, not solely a processing role. Over 12 months, you'll document how payroll operates in each country, establish and train a primary and backup owner for every country, move all payroll onto a global operating model, and hand over the result to a permanent team, supported by a costed recommendation on how that team should be structured.
You'll work alongside the Global Payroll Manager and the Payroll Specialist, with sponsorship from the VP People Services.
The focus will be on building the new operating model during the first eight months. Your responsibility for running payroll will grow through the final phase, culminating in running payroll for all 14 countries on the new model.
What You'll Be Responsible For
1. Global Payroll Operating Model
• Lead the move of all 14 countries onto the global payroll operating model.

• Define and embed workflows between HR Operations, Finance and HRBPs.

• Strengthen and deliver the service catalogue.

2. Process Documentation & Assessment
• Document processes, calendars, cut-offs, approvals, provider interfaces and controls for each country, starting with the five priority countries.

• Capture volume and productivity data to inform the sizing of the permanent team.

3. Ownership & Continuity
• Establish a named primary owner and a trained backup for every country.

• Secure time commitments from current owners, scheduled around payroll cut-offs.

• Train backups to run each payroll.

4. Payroll Operations
• Ensure accurate, timely and compliant payroll processing, reconciliations, audits and issue resolution alongside the existing team.

• Build towards running payroll for all 14 countries by the end of the contract.

5. Capability Building
• Upskill colleagues where required on the documented model, ensuring knowledge sits with the permanent team and not with the postholder.

6. Controls & Governance
• Build documented approvals and independent reviews into each country process so Finance and auditors can evidence repeatable controls.

• Maintain regulatory compliance, statutory filing discipline and legislative awareness across jurisdictions.

7. Provider Management
• Produce a single view of how each country operates and what each provider does, establishing the baseline for a later, separate decision on provider consolidation.

8. Automation & Self-Service
• Specify self-service and automation use cases for Luna, HiBob, HR Hub and Jira ticketing systems, built on documented and standardised processes.

9. Payroll Onboarding Playbook
• Produce a standard payroll onboarding playbook so that an acquisition or new country can be absorbed into the model rather than set up with another provider and another individual owner.

10. Benefits Ways of Working
• Support the move of benefits administration individual HR Operations and payroll owners to a global operating model by capturing the as-is and setting up structured ways of working.

• Benefits management remains in HR Operations.

11. Reporting & Analytics
• Establish reporting on payroll corrections and off-cycle payments, where there is no visibility today.

• Report on progress against the delivery plan to the VP People Services.

12. Permanent Structure & Handover
• Provide the as-is, the to-be and the full cost, with a recommendation on the permanent payroll structure, for the leadership decision gate.

• Complete the handover to permanent hires with an overlap period.

13. Stakeholder Partnership
• Act as the payroll SME and collaborate across HR Operations, HRBPs, Finance, Legal, IT, country payroll owners and providers.

Your First 12 Months
The role has a clear delivery roadmap, with a focus on building the operating model before taking full ownership of payroll operations.
Months 1–3 | Capture the As-Is
• Document processes, calendars, cut-offs, approvals, provider interfaces and controls for Australia, Norway, Poland, Tunisia and France.

• Name a primary and a backup owner for each country.

• Establish baseline volumes and productivity.

• Build the plan to move all countries to the global operating model.

• Present a progress checkpoint to leadership at month 3.

Months 4–8 | Move to the Model
• Work with the VP People Services to implement workflows between HR Operations, Finance and HRBPs.

• Embed the workflows and deliver a service catalogue.

• Move payroll onto the global operating model.

• Build the capability of the existing team.

Months 9–12 | Extend & Hand Over
• Extend the model to the remaining countries.

• Specify self-service and automation use cases for Luna, HiBob and HR Hub.

• Run payrolls for all 14 countries.

• Complete the handover to permanent hires with an overlap period.

• Deliver a recommendation on the permanent team structure.

What We're Looking For
• Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.

• 7+ years of payroll experience in a complex, multi-country environment.

• 2+ years leading payroll projects or process improvements.

• Demonstrated experience running payroll across multiple countries and delivery models, including outsourced, EOR or PEO providers.

• Experience documenting payroll processes and designing controls to audit standard.

• Strong knowledge of payroll regulations and tax requirements.

• Experience with payroll systems, ideally ADP, Deel and HiBob.

• Ability to build capability in colleagues and secure time from stakeholders who do not report to the role.

• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills.

Nice to Have
• CPP, FPC, PMP, Agile, or similar certifications.

• Merger and acquisition or new-country payroll onboarding experience.

• Experience specifying self-service or automation use cases for HRIS and payroll platforms.

Key Skills & Competencies
• Payroll Administration

• Operating Model Design & Documentation

• Project Management

• Process Improvement

• Multi-Country & Provider Management

• Capability Building & Handover

• Stakeholder Management

• Compliance, Controls & Risk Management

• Data Analysis & Reporting

What Success Looks Like
By the end of the 12-month contract, success will mean:
• 14 out of 14 countries have a documented payroll manual and are aligned with the global operating model.

• 14 out of 14 countries have a named primary owner and a trained backup.

• The as-is documentation and named primary and backup owners are in place for the five priority countries by the month 3 checkpoint.

• Workflows between HR Operations, Finance and HRBPs are live, with a service catalogue in use.

• Full visibility of payroll corrections and off-cycle payments, with a 2% global error rate target.

• Positive audit and compliance outcomes.

Job Description:
Customer Experience Strategist
CX, Service Design & UX | UK Hybrid

We’re looking for a Customer Experience Strategist to join Remedy Edge’s growing Experience team.

This is a hands-on strategy role sitting across customer experience, service design, digital product thinking and UX.

You’ll help us understand what patients, HCPs and other healthcare audiences need, identify where experiences aren’t working, and translate those insights into better journeys, services, tools and digital experiences.

What makes the role different?
Our Experience team often works upstream of traditional creative and production.

One project might involve understanding friction across a complex patient or HCP journey and redesigning the service around it. Another might involve helping define a new digital tool, platform or support experience, developing its architecture and user flows, prototyping how it could work and testing the concept before it moves into full design and build.

So we’re looking for someone comfortable moving between: research → CX strategy → service design → UX → prototypes → testing.

You won’t need to be a UI designer or developer. But you should understand experience and UX deeply enough to help define what should be created, why it matters and how it should work.

What you’ll be doing:
· Develop customer journeys and experience strategies.
· Identify customer needs, behaviours, barriers and opportunities.
· Create journey maps, service blueprints and future-state experiences.
· Help design new services, tools and digital experiences.
· Develop UX principles, information architecture and user flows.
· Work with wireframes and prototypes to make ideas tangible.
· Contribute to concept and usability testing.
· Facilitate workshops and confidently work directly with clients.
· Collaborate with designers, creatives, technologists and developers.
· Work on global programmes that create master experiences for local markets to adopt and adapt.
· Contribute to pitches and the continued growth of Remedy Edge’s Experience offer.

What we’re looking for:
You will have extensive relevant experience across areas such as Experience Strategy, CX, service design, UX strategy, digital product or service design, or digital transformation.

You’ll have strong human-centred thinking and be comfortable taking work from an ambiguous customer problem towards a practical experience solution.

We’d particularly like to see experience in:
· Customer or user research.
· Journey mapping.
· Service design.
· UX principles.
· Information architecture and user flows.
· Wireframes or prototyping.
· Client-facing strategy and workshops.
· Collaborating with design and technology teams.

Experience with Figma or similar design and prototyping tools is useful. Curiosity about AI-enabled prototyping and new ways of making and testing ideas is encouraged.

Healthcare experience would be helpful, but it isn’t essential. We’re also interested in people from agencies and consultancies working across complex, service-led or regulated industries.

Why Remedy Edge?
We’re building Experience as a strategic capability that connects CX, service design, product thinking and UX, rather than treating UX simply as downstream design or production.

That means you’ll get the opportunity to help clients decide what experience should exist and how it should work, then make that strategy tangible enough to prototype, test and ultimately build.

The PMO Analyst provides practical day-to-day support to the programme and its workstreams, helping to maintain reliable plans, controls and governance information. The role will report to a senior member of the PMO team and work closely with Project Managers, Programme Managers and Workstream Leads to track delivery, improve the quality of reporting and ensure that risks, issues, actions and dependencies are actively managed.

This is a hands-on coordination role suited to someone developing their career in project or programme management. The postholder will be expected to work with detail, follow up constructively, challenge information where it is unclear or incomplete, and escalate material concerns promptly.

About the Job

While there is rarely a typical day, here’s a snapshot of some of the key parts of the job:

 Transition Planning and Change Control
• Maintain and consolidate the integrated transition plan, ensuring workstream updates are reflected accurately and on time.
• Track milestones, deliverables, dependencies and critical path activities, highlighting slippage or emerging delivery risks.
• Review plan updates for quality and consistency, challenge gaps or conflicting information, and follow up actions to closure.
• Support change control by recording proposed changes, assessing impacts with the relevant owners, maintaining the change log and tracking decisions.
• Maintain clear version control and an auditable record of approved baseline changes.

RAID and Action Management
• Maintain workstream and programme-level risk, assumption, issue and dependency logs, including ownership, target dates, status and mitigating actions.
• Consolidate workstream RAID information and identify items requiring cross-workstream coordination or programme-level visibility.
• Monitor overdue actions and changes in exposure, follow up with owners and escalate material items to the relevant Programme Manager.
• Support the preparation of RAID summaries for governance reporting and meetings.
• Promote consistent use of agreed RAID definitions, templates and escalation routes.

Workstream and Project Manager Support
• Support Project Managers and Workstream Leads in maintaining detailed workstream plans and coordinating day-to-day delivery activities.
• Undertake quality control of plans, reports and control information before submission for review or consolidation.
• Work with workstream leads to identify where delivery tolerances are at risk and ensure recovery actions are recorded and monitored.
• Coordinate inputs from multiple contributors and help resolve gaps, inconsistencies or late submissions.
• Support resource and capacity tracking, including requirements, constraints and impacts on delivery of the plan.
• Escalate material issues, dependencies and resource constraints to Programme Managers in a timely manner.

Reporting and Governance
• Prepare workstream status reporting for review and approval by the relevant Workstream Lead or Project Manager.
• Consolidate updates into clear programme reporting, including milestones, RAG status, achievements, upcoming activities, decisions and escalations.
• Attend joint working groups and legal entity-specific working group sessions, providing PMO support as required.
• Prepare agendas, capture concise minutes, decisions and actions, and circulate outputs promptly following meetings.
• Maintain governance calendars, meeting records, decision logs and supporting documentation in the agreed repository.
• Support the preparation and quality assurance of materials for working groups and other programme governance forums.

PMO Standards and Continuous Improvement 
• Apply agreed PMO standards, templates and controls consistently across assigned workstreams.
• Maintain accurate records and audit trails, ensuring information is accessible, current and appropriately controlled.
• Identify opportunities to simplify PMO processes, improve data quality and strengthen the usefulness of management information.
• Provide flexible PMO support across the programme in response to changing priorities.

Key Deliverables

• An accurate and current consolidated transition plan, supported by clear version and change control.
• Complete and actively managed workstream and programme RAID logs, action logs and decision records.
• Timely, quality-checked workstream and programme status reporting.
• Clear meeting agendas, minutes, decisions and actions for assigned governance forums.
• Up-to-date resource and capacity information linked to delivery requirements.
• Well-maintained PMO documentation and audit trails.

What you’ll need:

Essential:
• Experience supporting projects, programmes or a PMO environment, gained through employment, an internship, a placement or a comparable role.
• Strong organisation skills, with the ability to manage detail, deadlines and multiple inputs.
• Confidence following up actions and constructively challenging incomplete or inconsistent information.
• Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce concise minutes and status updates.
• Working knowledge of project controls, including plans, milestones, risks, issues, actions and dependencies.
• Good Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint and Word skills; experience using collaboration and document management tools.
• Attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate, high-quality outputs.
• Ability to build effective working relationships with Project Managers, Workstream Leads and wider stakeholders.

Desirable:
• Experience supporting a transformation, transition or operating model programme.
• Exposure to integrated planning, change control or resource and capacity tracking.
• Experience preparing materials for governance forums or senior stakeholders.
• Familiarity with project planning or portfolio management tools.
• A project management or PMO qualification, or active study towards one, such as APM, PRINCE2 or an equivalent (desireable)

About the role

WHAT YOU WILL OWN

You'll own one Pivotal program end to end, most likely the Biodefense Fellowship or the AI Uplift Program. You decide who the program is for, what it should achieve and how we measure that, and you are accountable for its results. You'll lead the Research Managers who work on your program.

Outside Pivotal, you represent the program: you recruit its mentors and partners, and you speak for it to funders and the field. You'll own:

 - Strategy and design. Decide who the program is for, what it should achieve, and how we measure that. Set its yearly plan and budget with our CEO.

 - Results. Track fellows' research and career outcomes, review each cohort, and improve the next one.

 - Mentors and partners. Recruit mentors, advisors and partner organisations for the program.

 - The program team. Lead the Research Managers who work on your program.

 - External relationships. Represent the program to partners, funders and the field.


WHO DOES WELL IN THIS ROLE

 - You have led a program, product or team.

 - You know the program's field & its people well.

 - Strong judgement about which work matters most for reducing catastrophic risk.

 - Experience managing people.

 - You are decisive, honest and direct.

 - You use AI well, and you know where it does not help.

 - You care about reducing catastrophic risks from AI. You do not need a research background.

We don’t expect anyone to be strong in all of this. If the role excites you, please apply, even if you match only part of what we describe here.


HOW WE HIRE

 - Written application. A short form and your CV. It takes about 30 minutes.

 - Automated video interview. About 10 minutes. You record short answers to a few questions, at a time that suits you.

 - Work task. About 2 hours, based on real work in this role. We pay you for this time. You may use AI tools, as you would in the job. Tell us which ones you used and how.

 - Personal interview. About 45 minutes. We discuss your work task and how you would approach the role. With your consent, we record it so that more of the team can review it.

 - Work trial and references. Up to three paid days working with us at our office in London. We also speak to two referees, after asking you.

Primer is the unified infrastructure for global payments. We give finance and payments teams the visibility and control to reduce complexity, improve performance, and capture more revenue - all from a single platform.

You'll join Tech as a Senior Engineer. Tech owns identity and access, IT and workplace technology for the whole company. You’d be working in conjunction with our Workplace Tech Engineer and IAM Engineer, helping shape the direction of the team as it grows.

This is a hands-on role. You'll work the access and IT queue with the team, and you'll lead the technical work that shrinks it: the automation, the identity platform and the roadmap. As Primer grows and the team grows with it, there's room for the role to grow too, including into leading the team for the right person.

Tech is an enablement team. It sits alongside Security Engineering, not inside it, and owns the request queue and the tools that keep everyone at Primer productive. Primer is growing fast, and access requests are growing even faster. Our job is to make getting the right access quick, safe and mostly automatic, so people can get on with their work and our security engineers can get back to security.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Work the IAM, IT and Workplace Tech queue alongside the team, and set the bar for turnaround and quality.

 - Keep access controls audit-ready. Work with Security and GRC on access reviews, least privilege and evidence for PCI DSS and SOC 2.

 - Partner with Security Engineering on the calls that need them, such as privileged access and policy exceptions, and handle the rest within Tech.

 - Mentor the other engineers on the team, review their work and share what you know.

 - Track and report on how the queue is doing: volume, turnaround, and how much automation is taking off it.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Senior-level experience in IT, IAM or corporate engineering at a fast-growing tech company

 - Experience scaling an IT function through a period of fast headcount growth

We believe the future is all about autonomous websites and hyper-personalised user journeys.
We're building the Autonomous Website Experience. Today you choose tools, model content, write code, and fix bugs by hand. Tomorrow you say what you want, and the system builds, fixes, and improves the site with you, from the first demo to the daily updates.

The Tools and Activation Team
Our mission: build the tools that let developers, marketers, and AI agents, use Prismic efficiently, and design the most frictionless onboarding for different personalities and personas.
We own two sides of that problem.
• The tools. The CLI and MCP are how agents work with Prismic. An agent in Cursor, Claude, ChatGPT, or Codex should be able to do everything you can do in the UI, without guessing, getting stuck, or inventing glue code. The developer tooling is what closes the loop - how developers deliver slices and manage their day to day work. We make those surfaces reliable, complete, and efficient.

• The first mile. People don't just arrive from different places. They also arrive with different experience and different knowledge of Prismic. Everyone should be able to onboard. We design those paths for that range of people, and we are responsible for making them the best.

What we measure
We measure two things.
Activation with our tools. How many developers and agents activate with the MCP, whether they stay, and how often they come back.
Onboarding to production. How many people start with Prismic and deploy their website to production.

The problems you'd pick up
Here's what's actually on the table right now.
CLI and MCP that make humans and agents first-class users of Prismic. The CLI is how agents set up projects, model content, and stay in the codebase. The MCP is how they read, edit, and operate on content. Together they should cover the full surface of the product, not a thin slice of it. The hard part is not exposing an API. It is making people and agents efficient: the right tools, the right defaults, the right errors, and a path that doesn't fall apart past the happy path.
Developer tooling that stays out of the way. This is how developers actually interact with Prismic day to day: scaffolding projects, modeling data, developing Slices and syncing with remote server. You would help shape that interactions so people can do their work without fighting the tool.
Onboarding that works for different people. People arrive from different sources and they arrive with very different experience. All of them should be able to onboard. You would help design those paths and keep them coherent.

Why this role is interesting
• You build the technology, and you build it fast. We prototype quickly, learn from it, and keep what works. An idea goes from POC to something customers use without a long chain of handoffs.

• You talk to customers directly. Product Engineers here don't wait for a spec. You talk to users, decide what to build, ship it, and see whether it moved the numbers.

• Your users are humans and agents. Designing for developers, marketers, and AI agents at once is a new problem. There is no established playbook, so you help write it.

• Your impact is easy to see. Activation and websites in production are numbers you can watch move because of what you shipped.

Role 💫
We're looking for a Senior Product Engineer to join the Tools and Activation Team.
We chose the title Product Engineer on purpose. We're not looking for someone who ships clean code against a spec. We want someone who owns the outcome: talks to users, decides what to build with product, ships it, and is accountable for whether it moved the numbers. It's less about handoffs and more about owning the work end to end.
This is an individual contributor role. You'll have a lot of autonomy over both product and technical decisions, while working closely with product, design, and the rest of the engineering team.

Are you the one? 🧠
This role leans backend. You will spend most of your time on services, APIs and CLIs. Frontend is part of the job when the path to activation lives in a UI, but it is not the centre of gravity.
Ideally, you:
• Are a strong backend engineer in TypeScript, comfortable designing APIs and CLIs

• Have built developer-facing surfaces like CLIs or SDKs. You’re used to commands that compose, contracts that stay stable, output that tells you what to do next, and errors specific enough to recover from.

• Have built agent-facing surfaces before. The client of our products is not always a human. Agents get stuck on interactive prompts, vague errors, and incomplete tools. You understand the problems and know how to solve them.

• Are at home with ambiguous problems and short feedback loops. You can take an idea to a POC quickly, learn from it, and decide what to keep.

You also bring the baseline every Product Engineer here shares:
• You're full-stack enough to work across the stack when the problem requires it, including databases and infrastructure.

• You handle complex integrations and product problems without waiting to be told what to do.

• You have hands-on experience with agentic AI systems, or strong curiosity about them.

• You care about quality engineering: testing, observability, traceability.

We weigh competencies over years of experience or job titles.

Bonus points
• You've shipped or maintained an MCP server, or a CLI designed for both humans and agents.

• You've worked on developer experience in a product company.

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. We care about how you think, how you build, and how you raise the level of the system around you.

THE TEAM

Every courier who works with Relay chooses their day. A day is a set of routes that have to fit together, and every courier's ideal day competes with everyone else's. Work is finite and every route still has to be covered, so matching thousands of couriers to the work they want is a recommendation problem with few precedents.

Science at Relay is the brain of the operation: machine learning, operational research, recommender systems, causal inference, location intelligence and experimentation, working together to decide how every parcel gets delivered. There's no existing recommender to iterate on. You'll build it.


RECOMMENDER SYSTEMS HIGHLIGHTS

 - Combinatorial, constrained and competitive: every recommendation has to be feasible for the whole network, not just right for one courier.

 - Your models power large-scale optimisation that balances thousands of couriers' preferences against the constraints of a physical network.

 - Price is part of the recommendation, so economics, personalisation and optimisation have to work as one.

 - Our apps collect millions of data points every day.

 - Set the standard for recommender systems at Relay.

 - Lead the evolution of Relay's recommender from research to production.

 - Design and build the recommender systems that power Relay's key decisions.

 - Partner with Operational Research to unite recommender models and optimisation.

 - Contribute to Relay's research culture, and develop our voice in the tech community.

Every courier who works with Relay chooses their day. A day is a set of routes that have to fit together, and every courier's ideal day competes with everyone else's. Work is finite and every route still has to be covered, so matching thousands of couriers to the work they want is a recommendation problem with few precedents.

Science at Relay is the brain of the operation: machine learning, operational research, recommender systems, causal inference, location intelligence and experimentation, working together to decide how every parcel gets delivered. There's no existing recommender to iterate on. You'll build it.

 - Combinatorial, constrained and competitive: every recommendation has to be feasible for the whole network, not just right for one courier.

 - Your models power large-scale optimisation that balances thousands of couriers' preferences against the constraints of a physical network.

 - Price is part of the recommendation, so economics, personalisation and optimisation have to work as one.

 - Our apps collect millions of data points every day.

About Rivian

Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. 
As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. 

Role Summary

As a Lead Learning Experience Designer, you’ll create learning experiences that help Rivian’s Sales, Service, and Delivery teams build skills, develop confidence, and deliver thoughtful customer experiences.
We’re evolving how learning experiences are designed and built. We’re looking for someone at the forefront of applying AI to learning design—someone who actively experiments, brings strong instructional judgment, and turns new capabilities into high-quality training. You’ll use AI to expand what we can create, from realistic scenarios and interactive content to games, simulations, and tools that support employees on the job.
This is a hands-on role with broad ownership. You’ll lead complex learning projects, partner closely with the business, and help the team develop new ways of working. Curiosity matters, along with the ability to take an idea through testing, refinement, and delivery.

Responsibilities

Drive complete learning programs, partnering with stakeholders to identify performance needs and lead learning projects from discovery through launch and improvement.
Create clear, practical learning across formats, including digital courses, facilitated experiences, interactions, games, simulations, and performance support.
Use AI to explore, prototype, and produce high-quality learning, applying careful review for accuracy, instructional value, accessibility, and Rivian’s voice.
Manage scope and dependencies with partners, communicate progress, and adapt to changing business needs.
Evolve team practices by testing new tools, sharing effective approaches, and coaching fellow designers.
Use feedback, assessments, and performance data to improve learning effectiveness.

Qualifications

A strong workplace learning portfolio demonstrating instructional judgment, creative execution, and high-quality writing.
Expertise in measuring learning effectiveness, skill application, and performance outcomes.
Hands-on experience applying AI to learning design and development, with examples of finished work and a habit of testing emerging capabilities.
Strong grounding in adult learning, performance consulting, and accessible design, including meaningful practice and feedback.
Experience leading complex projects, navigating ambiguity, and influencing stakeholders.
Proficiency with tools such as Articulate Rise 360 and Storyline, plus the ability to build beyond established formats.
Ability to explain design decisions, provide constructive feedback, and develop others’ skills.

Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers.
From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines.
What does the team work on?
This team spends most of its time working on customer focused features that improve the user experience, from content discovery and search to Roku pay and subscription to embedded software and firmware, and much more. Our product roadmap helps us accelerate our growth and scale, putting surprising new features into the hands of tens of millions of Roku users worldwide. Our developers and engineers are owners. They are motivated from within, finding and taking on a feature or project simply because that problem needs to be solved and shipped. But that individual must work together with different engineering teams, UI design, product teams, and business leadership to make things happen, which means that engineers succeed here because they can maintain that independent spirit and motivation within a deeply collaborative environment. We are the pragmatic dreamers inventing and re-inventing the world of streaming media.
What is the role?
As a Senior Software Engineer on the OS UI/SDK team, you will design, develop, and deliver engaging platform features — including screensavers, static and dynamic wallpapers, trivia, featured experiences, and AI-driven content initiatives — that reach millions of Roku users worldwide. You will leverage AI and machine learning technologies to develop new capabilities that enhance user experiences across the Roku platform. This role requires a proactive, ownership-driven approach where you will create proof-of-concept prototypes in a startup-minded environment and then adapt those prototypes for production-grade deployment. You will collaborate closely with cross-functional partners in UI/UX design, product management, backend engineering, and business leadership to translate ideas into impactful solutions. You will investigate, diagnose, and resolve technical issues to maintain high-quality, commercially viable products. This is an opportunity to shape the future of streaming entertainment through innovation and a deep commitment to engineering excellence.
How will I use AI at Roku?
At Roku, we don't just use AI, we work with it. AI agents and smart tools help power drafts, analysis, and repetitive workflows, while our people bring direction, judgment, and accountability. We're looking for curious, adaptable builders who can show how they've used AI or automation to move faster, raise the bar, and scale their impact.
We value your AI skills if have built fluency across the agentic engineering toolchain — coding harnesses like Claude Code or Cursor, MCP servers, custom skills, or agent frameworks. And you can describe projects where you shipped real work with these tools. You know how to drive an agent, verify its output, and ramp on an unfamiliar codebase with an agent helping you.

Design and develop features for new experiences on the Roku platform, including screensavers, wallpapers, trivia, and featured experiences
Build proof-of-concept prototypes to validate ideas rapidly, working with a startup mindset to iterate quickly and deliver solutions
Collaborate with UI/UX design, backend engineering, and product management teams to create and implement new user experiences
Adapt proof-of-concept solutions into production-ready, scalable implementations
Leverage AI, machine learning, and large language model technologies to develop innovative platform features
Investigate, diagnose, and resolve technical issues to maintain commercially viable solutions
Contribute to API design decisions, understanding considerations and trade-offs
Work across cloud development, content management, and UI development to deliver end-to-end feature solutions
What experience would help someone be successful in this role at Roku?
Extensive experience in a software engineering environment
Demonstrated project work using AI/ML and LLM technologies
Proficiency in scripting languages such as JavaScript, TypeScript, React Native, Python, BrightScript, or related technologies
Experience working in an embedded environment
Experience in productionising solutions, including content management, UI development, cloud development, and cloud backend integration
Knowledge of core OS concepts such as memory management and multi-threading
Experience in API design, with an understanding of considerations and trade-offs
Strong communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across teams
Consumer electronics experience in media, content, or ad product development is a plus
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field

• Support and align our specialised designers - framework and embedded - around a consistent experience across modules and applications

• Communicate UX principles and investment priorities to senior leadership, demonstrating the value and potential impact of UX-related roadmap items

• Produce high-level experience flows and service blueprints that connect journeys across applications and domains

• Review Design System and module deliverables for alignment with experience strategy and brand

• Support embedded designers from discovery through to delivery by co-framing problems, reviewing flows against the cross-application blueprint and ensuring continuity across user journeys

• Set KPIs and use analytics, user research, A/B tests and competitive analysis to inform and refine design decisions

• Promote a UX culture centred on user needs, inclusive design and accessibility standards such as WCAG across the organisation

• Collaborate with Marketing on tone, terminology and brand consistency across products

• Strong experience leading discovery, from understanding user needs through research and prototyping to defining and refining UX solutions

• Advanced proficiency in Figma, with experience creating and iterating wireframes, mock-ups and prototypes

• Experience bringing together multiple designers, including without formal reporting lines, to create a consistent experience across products or modules

This is a high-profile role within the business. The ideal candidate is comfortable in operating in an environment where there isn’t a pre-existing “playbook”, putting their experience into practice to closely work with the Smiths business to achieve practical, pragmatic and sustainable improvements in internal controls. The role holder will work closely with the IT function (BIS), divisional and site IT teams, and external stakeholders (e.g., consultants and external auditors) in advancing the organisation’s use of AI & Analytics tools to meet control requirements and implement all the tools, techniques, and resources to ensure these are met sustainably. The ideal candidate for this position will have prior experience of delivering AI & Analytics solutions in the internal audit and internal control fields for a large corporation or as a consultant with a top-tier practice firm. In addition, they will have experience designing and implementing General IT and automated controls leveraging technology, standardisation, and continuous improvement. You will master excellent AI and data analytics skills, hold a qualification with CISA/CISM or similar and preferably be a qualified accountant (ACA/ACCA) with experience with external audit. AI & Analytics

General IT Controls

• Understanding prospective customers' commercial and operational challenges, translating their requirements into compelling technology solutions and business cases.

• Developing and maintaining a high-quality sales pipeline, with accurate CRM records, forecasting and clear visibility of opportunities, risks and next steps.

• Collaborating with colleagues across Growth & Commercial to share market intelligence, coordinate client engagement and maximise collective commercial success.

• Supporting the transition of new clients into implementation and onboarding, ensuring commercial commitments and expectations are clearly communicated.
