We are looking for a technology leader with strong commercial awareness who understands software delivery and emerging technology, but starts with the needs of the business. You will lead our Digital Products and Technology function, working closely with Client Services, Operations, Production, Creative and other teams. You will understand their pressures, challenge established practices where there is a better way and help colleagues adopt change with confidence. 

Our function brings together Quest, our business-critical management information system and its Workday integration; an established 3D spatial capture and LiDAR team; and a digital content and LED team. You do not need to be the technical expert in every area. You do need the judgement to lead different specialists, connect their work to business priorities and improve what they deliver for our clients. 

Above all, we want someone who will strengthen a technology function that colleagues trust, value and want to work with, while helping LIVE·TEAM innovate, grow and stay competitive. 

WHAT YOU WILL LEAD:

1. Quest development team

Quest is LIVE·TEAM’s internally developed management information (MI) system, underpinning our day-to-day operation and integrating with Workday. The MVP is defined and development is underway with an external partner and internal colleagues, targeting early January 2027. Depending on recruitment timing, the programme may be moving into rollout, training and ongoing development. The AVP will need to take ownership of the programme at whichever stage it has reached, rather than restart work already agreed.

• Own technical delivery of Quest, including sprint progress, engineering quality, testing, integrations, dependencies, release readiness, supplier performance and ongoing support. 
• Agree product priorities and roadmap decisions with business owners. They help determine what matters most; you are accountable for planning and delivering the technical work, explaining risks, costs and trade-offs clearly. 
• Bring end-to-end software delivery knowledge, from requirements, user journeys and backlog management through development, quality assurance, user acceptance testing, release, adoption and ongoing improvement. 
• Manage the external development partner and internal teams effectively, challenging estimates and decisions where needed without taking over the work of specialist developers. 
• After MVP, work with business leaders to deliver new modules and improvements that make company-wide working practices better, differentiate LIVE·TEAM, improve efficiency and create new revenue opportunities. 
• Oversee the transition from development into rollout, user training, adoption and ongoing enhancement as the programme progresses. Keep Quest secure, reliable and well supported, with clear ownership of data, integrations and documentation. 

2. AI, automation and future business capability

AI and automation will change how we work and what clients expect from us. We need a leader who can spot useful opportunities, work closely with colleagues to define the problem properly, and move quickly from an idea to a dependable tool that can be used by our teams or clients. Just as importantly, they must help LIVE·TEAM prepare for changes ahead without chasing technology for its own sake.

• Build an AI and automation roadmap tied to commercial goals, client delivery, operational capacity, quality and competitiveness. 
• Work directly with Client Services, Operations, Production, Creative, Studio, Finance and other teams. Listen carefully, understand the business objective, test assumptions and challenge the brief constructively until there is a shared, clear definition of the problem and what success looks like. 
• Rapidly prototype AI-enabled software and operational tools using appropriate development and AI platforms. Be capable of hands-on experimentation, then lead the work through testing, refinement and delivery of a secure, reliable, client-ready or business-ready solution, built via internal development team or if required with a development partner. 
• Explore and implement improvements in artworking and artwork adaptation, image creation, asset handling, approvals, reporting, information retrieval and repetitive administrative work. 
• Look beyond cost savings. Work with business leaders to understand how AI may change our services, delivery model and client expectations, and where we should invest or build new capabilities to protect and grow our position. 
• Test prototypes with the people who will use them, refine them against real workflows and take viable solutions through to supported production use. Establish ownership, training, maintenance and measures of value; stop initiatives that do not deliver. 
• Manage risks around intellectual property, client confidentiality, data protection, security, accuracy and human oversight. 
• Keep colleagues informed about useful developments in plain language, and work with THE.TEAM Central IT on AI, security, policy and scale. 

3. Working with our people and delivering change

LIVE·TEAM is a fast-moving, client-led business. Deadlines, production peaks and client commitments cannot simply be moved to suit a technology timetable. Our technology team must work within that cadence, while maintaining appropriate standards for quality, security and reliability.

• Be visible and approachable. Listen to the people doing the work before recommending changes, and explain technical choices without jargon. 
• Plan development, releases, testing and training with business leads to minimise disruption and avoid unnecessary administration. 
• Bring colleagues into the design, testing and rollout of solutions. Provide practical, inclusive support for people with different levels of technical confidence so nobody is left behind. 
• Challenge inefficient practices with evidence, empathy and persistence. Sometimes the business will need encouragement to adopt a better approach; change should be agreed and supported, not imposed. 
• Build a responsive, accountable technology team that people across LIVE·TEAM find easy to work with. Measure success through adoption, service and business results, not just completed technical milestones. 

4. Representing LIVE·TEAM across THE·TEAM

LIVE·TEAM operates within the wider THE·TEAM group, which provides centralised IT services, technology infrastructure, security standards and group-wide policies. The AVP will work closely with THE·TEAM's central IT function to ensure LIVE·TEAM benefits from shared technology, expertise and governance, while representing and protecting the specific operational, commercial and client requirements of our business. This includes ensuring LIVE·TEAM is actively involved in relevant technology decisions and that any adoption of group-wide systems, platforms or policies is considered in consultation with our business leaders, with a clear understanding of the practical impact on our teams and how we deliver for clients. 

• Stay close to wider THE·TEAM technology plans and ensure LIVE·TEAM has a meaningful voice early in relevant discussions and decisions. 
• Represent our operational, creative, client and commercial requirements, including dependencies around QUEST and other systems. 
• Assess proposed group platforms and standards with LIVE·TEAM business leads before adoption, considering fit, integration, cost, disruption, security and long-term value. 
• Work constructively with wider group colleagues, sharing good ideas and avoiding duplication while protecting the needs of our business. 
• Introduce agreed group solutions through proper consultation, clear ownership, communication, testing and support.

5. Leading specialist teams and delivery partners

• Lead internal specialists and external partners with clear priorities, realistic budgets, accountability and an approachable service culture. 
• Lead and support the established 3D spatial capture and LiDAR team, helping it improve its capabilities, connect more closely with operational and client-facing teams, and develop spatial capture into a stronger offering for LIVE·TEAM clients. Specialist depth is not required, but commercial knowledge and the ability to guide the team are essential. 
• Work with Client Services and commercial leads to identify where spatial capture can improve existing projects, create new services and generate revenue, while ensuring the team has the capacity, skills and support to deliver consistently. 
• Oversee governance, information security, data quality, integrations, resilience, supplier relationships and value for money, drawing on specialist expertise as needed. 
• Give senior leaders clear, candid updates on progress, investment, outcomes, risks and decisions required.

WHAT YOU WILL BRING:

Essential experience and approach

• Senior experience leading business-facing technology, digital product or software delivery in an operationally complex organisation. 
• Strong understanding of the full software development lifecycle, agile delivery, product roadmaps, integrations, testing, releases and ongoing development of business-critical systems after launch. 
• Experience managing external software development partners alongside internal teams, with a clear grasp of scope, delivery quality, commercial terms and accountability. 
• Practical experience of AI-enabled software prototyping and automation, with the ability to turn a clear business brief into a working proof of concept and guide it through to a reliable operational product, using internal teams or partners as appropriate. 
• Enough hands-on software development or engineering experience to assess technical feasibility, build or adapt prototypes, challenge implementation choices and work credibly with developers. Deep expertise in every technology used by LIVE·TEAM is not expected. 
• A track record of turning business needs into solutions that people use and that deliver measurable results. 
• An approachable, curious and commercially aware leadership style. You can challenge technical specialists and hold them accountable, while being equally comfortable with project managers, artworkers, operations teams and client services colleagues.

Your features move a measurable metric. Engineers are unblocked because your requirements and decisions are clear. You’ll be the go-to person for your product area and ready to own a full roadmap.

About the role

We are looking for a detail-driven and proactive Finance Operations Analyst to join our finance team. This is a key operational role supporting the end-to-end finance function, with a primary focus on billing, accounts receivable and accounts payable. The role combines hands-on operational delivery with practical financial analysis, using data to investigate issues, prioritise action and enhance the efficiency and accuracy of finance processes. 

Accuracy, pace and ownership are essential in this role. You will play a critical part in ensuring revenue is billed accurately, supplier invoices are reviewed and processed efficiently, payments are made on time and working capital is effectively managed. Working closely with the Senior Management Accountant, Financial Controller and wider finance team, you will help deliver smooth day-to-day finance operations, maintain strong financial controls, and support healthy cash flow. Alongside daily processing, you will analyse billing, overdue debt and payment issues, discuss findings directly with senior finance colleagues, and support reconciliations and month-end reporting. 

This role offers an excellent opportunity to develop broad finance operations experience, contribute to process improvements and build a strong foundation for progression within the finance team. During the six-month contract, you will help deliver a focused set of practical improvements to workflows and reporting, with clear documentation to support consistent ways of working across the team.

What you’ll do

**Billing & Accounts Receivable (AR)** 

- Raise accurate and timely client invoices in line with contracts and billing schedules
- Ensure all billable work and expenses is invoiced completely and accurately
- Manage the end-to-end accounts receivable process, including cash allocation and client account reconciliations
- Manage overdue debt by proactively chasing outstanding invoices to maximise cash collections
- Work with Client Partners and clients to obtain purchase orders, resolve billing queries and support timely invoicing
- Prepare and maintain aged debt reporting, providing insights into overdue balances, collection performance and accounts receivable trends (e.g. DSO, accrued revenue)

**Accounts Payable (AP)** 

- Review, code and process supplier invoices accurately, ensuring appropriate approvals are obtained and VAT is correctly accounted for
- Match purchase orders, invoices and receipts, investigating and resolving discrepancies where needed
- Prepare and process supplier payment runs in line with agreed payment terms
- Manage company credit card transactions, ensuring spend is appropriately coded, supported by valid receipts and compliant with the company expense policy
- Maintain supplier records and respond to supplier queries in a timely manner
- Ensure adherence to internal controls and finance policies

**Expenses Processing** 

- Review and process employee expense claims in line with company policy
- Ensure all expenses are supported with appropriate documentation and approvals
- Reconcile expenses and credit card transactions within the accounting system, following up on outstanding documentation where required

**Transactional Finance & Operations**

- Support the month-end close process, including reconciliations and accruals where required
- Maintain accurate and complete financial records across AR, AP, expenses and cash
- Work closely with the Management Accountant and wider finance team to support accurate financial reporting
- Identify opportunities to improve processes, controls and system efficiencies

What a typical week could includeYou might start by reviewing receipts and overdue balances, following up customer queries and checking upcoming supplier payments, helping support cash flow and working capital. Alongside processing invoices and expenses, you could investigate a billing discrepancy, explain changes in aged debt and agree collection priorities directly with the Senior Management Accountant and Financial Controller. 

Around month-end, your focus will shift towards reconciliations and supporting schedules, helping maintain accurate records and strong financial controls. As operational priorities allow, you will contribute to practical improvements, such as simplifying a reconciliation or reducing manual steps in a report. 

Working closely with the wider finance team, you will have opportunities to learn and develop across accounts receivable, accounts payable and finance operations. The balance will vary with payment deadlines and the month-end cycle, offering varied, hands-on work where accuracy, ownership and continuous improvement are valued.

Who you are

- Experience in accounts receivable, accounts payable and finance operations
- Highly organised with excellent attention to detail and strong numerical accuracy
- Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, managing multiple priorities and deadlines
- Strong communication and relationship building skills, with the ability to work effectively with colleagues, clients and suppliers
- Proactive, reliable, and able to take ownership of daily finance processes
- Good understanding of finance systems and transactional workflows
- A collaborative team player with a willingness to support the wider Finance and Operations function
- A continuous improvement mindset, with a desire to simplify and automate processes to enhance the efficiency of the finance function.

The role
VSI's network supports our offices, studios, data centres, and cloud-connected environments worldwide. As our Network Infrastructure Manager, you will lead the strategy, design, security, resilience and day-to-day performance of this global network. Your work will help our teams deliver localisation services securely and reliably for some of the world's largest brands.
This is a hands-on leadership role. You will work closely with our Global Director of IT and Infrastructure to set global network standards, lead modernisation and upgrade programmes, and give a clear view of network health, capacity, risk and investment priorities. You will also lead and develop network team members and specialist partners to ensure every VSI location receives consistent support. You will work with colleagues in IT, Security, Content Security and studio operations, and with people across the wider business.
What you will do
• Set the network strategy. Own the global network roadmap, architecture principles, technical standards and reference designs. Turn business, studio, security, and growth needs into practical, easy-to-support solutions.

• Run day-to-day network services. Oversee local area network (LAN), wide area network (WAN), wireless, internet connectivity, remote access, routing, switching, Domain Name System (DNS), Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) and network management services. Keep them monitored, maintained and supported to agreed standards.

• Protect the network. Manage firewalls, access control, network segmentation, secure remote connectivity and administrative access. Find vulnerabilities, coordinate fixes and make sure configurations meet VSI's information security, content security and data protection obligations.

• Manage the infrastructure lifecycle. Plan and deliver the deployment, upgrade, replacement and decommissioning of core network equipment and firewalls across our locations. Keep versions supported, designs resilient, configurations standard, inventories accurate, and ensure the right vendor support is in place.

• Monitor performance and plan capacity. Set up meaningful monitoring, alerting and reporting on availability, utilisation, latency, packet loss, errors and capacity. Analyse trends, resolve performance issues and make evidence-based recommendations for improvement and investment.

• Build resilience. Design resilience that matches how critical each service is to the business. Support disaster recovery and business continuity planning by documenting dependencies, recovery procedures, and test scenarios, and by taking part in regular recovery and failover exercises.

• Manage changes and keep records current. Ensure every network change is risk-assessed, documented, tested, approved, communicated, and includes a rollback plan. Keep network diagrams, configuration standards, Internet Protocol (IP) address records, firewall documentation, procedures and support information up to date.

• Lead the response to major incidents. Provide technical leadership during high-severity network incidents. Coordinate internal teams and suppliers, keep stakeholders updated on impact and recovery, and ensure root causes are identified and corrective actions are completed.

• Lead the network side of projects. Lead the network workstream for office openings, relocations, acquisitions, studio changes, cloud connectivity and other infrastructure programmes. Define scope, dependencies, resources, risks, acceptance criteria and handover requirements.

• Manage suppliers and budgets. Manage network carriers, technology vendors and specialist partners against their contracts and service levels. Contribute to budget planning, forecasting and cost control, and look for ways to consolidate services, improve value and reduce risk.

• Track risk and support audits. Keep visibility of network risks, technical debt, exceptions and improvement actions. Provide evidence for internal, client and external audits of network infrastructure and security controls.

• Develop your team. Manage, mentor and develop network team members and technical colleagues across our locations. Set clear priorities and standards, encourage knowledge sharing, and make sure documentation and cross-training mean no service depends on one person.

• Communicate clearly. Build strong relationships with colleagues in IT, Security, Content Security, studio operations and the wider business. Explain technical issues, risks, options and recommendations to both technical and non-technical audiences.

What we are looking for
• Proven experience in hands-on network infrastructure management or senior network engineering across several sites.

• Strong knowledge of enterprise routing, switching, wireless networking, WAN connectivity, firewalls, virtual private networks (VPNs), network segmentation, access control lists (ACLs), and core services such as DNS and DHCP.

• Demonstrable experience designing, implementing and supporting Palo Alto firewalls and their security policy controls.

• Experience managing network monitoring, capacity, availability, lifecycle, configuration and operational documentation.

• Experience leading network incidents, technical changes, and infrastructure projects involving multiple stakeholders and suppliers.

• A practical understanding of information security, risk management, business continuity and audit requirements.

• Experience managing budgets, contracts, carriers and technology vendors.

• Clear written and verbal communication, sound judgement, and the confidence to influence stakeholders and challenge them constructively.

• An organised, collaborative leadership style, with the ability to set priorities, delegate effectively and develop technical staff.

It would be helpful if you have
• In-depth experience with both Palo Alto and Fortinet firewalls.

• A Palo Alto firewall certification.

• In-depth experience with Layer 2 switching and Layer 3 routing.

• Windows Server and Linux administration experience.

• Experience with storage platforms, ideally Qumulo, Nimble and Quantum Xcellis.

• Experience with Excel and Power BI.

• Strong command-line skills and scripting experience in Linux and PowerShell.

• Experience with Python.

• Knowledge of and experience with Amazon Web Services (AWS).

• A PRINCE2 project management qualification or equivalent.

Why join VSI?
At VSI, you will join a passionate, highly driven team helping entertainment travel the world. VSI is a leading localisation company. We provide foreign-language versioning services, including voice-over, dubbing, subtitling and translation, from dedicated facilities in the world's major media hubs. In this role, you will directly shape the secure, resilient connectivity our studios and colleagues rely on to deliver high-profile global content for some of the world's largest brands.
This role offers real scope and visible impact. You will lead network strategy across an international estate, guide new offices and studio changes, and build a team around you. We support people to grow their careers alongside experienced colleagues and some of the best talent in the localisation industry.

job_description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

Real estate is the physical foundation of Waymo’s operations. The Strategy team collaborates across functions to design the optimal future footprint, ensuring the Waymo driver operates safely and efficiently. As we scale into new markets, specialized analysis is essential to guiding our real estate strategy. In this role, you will directly influence the location, size, capacity, and design of all future operations facilities.

This role follows a hybrid work schedule and reports to the Real Estate Strategy Manager.

You will:

• Requirements Gathering: Formalize demand forecasts into detailed real estate requirement documents for expansion, consolidation, and sequencing.

• Data Stewardship: Manage the end-to-end life-cycle of portfolio data, ensuring high integrity in supply/demand metrics, KPIs, and market health reporting.

• Decision Documentation: Produce standardized reports and strategic briefings that translate complex analytics into actionable insights for leadership.

• Predictive Modeling: Build and maintain supply/demand models to generate the data-driven forecasts used for long-term strategic planning.

• Technical Liaison: Define and document technical requirements for the analytics team to ensure dashboards align with business strategy.

• Analytical Support: Execute data-heavy ad-hoc analysis to support business case development and multi-market occupier engagements.

You have:

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Real Estate, Finance, Information Systems, or a related quantitative field.

• Experience: 4 years of experience in data analysis, corporate real estate, or business intelligence.

• Technical Writing: Proven ability to create clear, concise documentation and process workflows.

• Analytical Rigor: Exceptional attention to detail with the ability to manage large datasets without compromising accuracy.

• Agility: Ability to pivot between deep-dive data tasks and collaborative project coordination in a fast-paced environment.

We prefer:

• Technical Stack: Advanced Excel, experience with SQL, Python, Looker

• Strategic Thinking & Financial Acumen

• Experienced Leadership & Development

• Client Relationship Management

• Experience with Data-Driven Decision Making

• Communication & Collaboration among teams and clients

Travel Requirement: 10%

• Occasional travel to New York City or San Francisco Bay Area

At Wise, our mission is Money Without Borders: instant, convenient, transparent and eventually free. As we grow and scale, we're looking for an experienced Finance Manager to join our Finance Risk and Controls team in London. You will help strengthen our internal control environment and deliver against US SOX requirements. You will also lead the controls work on some of our most important finance transformation projects.
You will work closely with Finance, Product, Procurement, Operations and Technology teams. You will embed a strong control culture that supports Wise's growth and doesn't add unnecessary bureaucracy.
Your Mission
• Create and advise on end-to-end process and control documentation: Build process maps and risk-control matrices where they don't exist. Advise process owners on keeping them accurate and current in line with SOX standards.

• Lead and support the implementation of new and improved processes and controls across Finance: Advise on identifying risks and designing and embedding controls across end-to-end processes. This includes fraud, payment, procurement, revenue and period-end accounting risks, and the IT dependencies.

• Own the accountability framework to support Financial Statement attestation: Set clear ownership, escalation routes and governance for controls across Group Finance for the business processes you cover.

• Be the point of contact for control testing: Coordinate with control owners, Internal Audit and External Audit. Help build and run a testing programme that independently assesses controls, identifies gaps and validates remediation.

• Support SOX readiness and remediation: Guide teams on US SOX and relevant local regulatory requirements. Drive the remediation of Material Weaknesses and the first-time implementation of controls.

• Manage the Finance Risk and Controls Self Assessment: Make sure it is completed accurately, on time and with clear follow-up on actions.

• Report to senior leadership: Report to the Finance Leadership Team and prepare material for the Operational Risk Committee. Present control performance, deficiencies, remediation progress and residual risk clearly and concisely.

• Partner with stakeholders across the business: Work with Finance, Risk, Internal Audit and non-Finance teams to set standards and policies. Develop KRIs to monitor risk on a continuous basis.

What you'll get from the role
• Real impact: You will shape how Wise implements SOX controls and remediates Material Weaknesses, and see the results.

• Visibility: You will regularly work with and present to senior leaders, including the Finance LT.

• Autonomy and ownership: You will have a high level of responsibility and the freedom to decide how best to deliver.

• Breadth of learning: You will gain in-depth knowledge of Wise's business by working with teams across Finance and the wider company.

• Room to grow: You will build your leadership skills by driving remediation with stakeholders across the business, in a fast-growing, global FinTech.

About you
Qualifications and experience
• You have a professional accounting qualification, such as US CPA, ACA, ACCA or an international equivalent.

• You have 8–10 years of experience in a similar role, in industry or at a Big 4 firm.

• You have a deep understanding of SOX controls and regulations, including financial statement assertions, key controls, and design and operating effectiveness.

• You have thorough process knowledge across areas such as Procurement, Revenue and HR.

• You have experience testing internal controls and evaluating deficiencies.

Skills and approach
• You communicate excellently, including with executive leadership. You explain technical issues in plain language and lead with the conclusions that matter.

• You work well with minimal direction in a fast-moving, less structured environment.

• You are pragmatic and commercially minded. You apply proportionate controls that balance risk against business practicality.

• You influence without relying on formal authority, and you stay calm when handling disagreement or resistance.

• You take ownership and see remediation through to completion.

• You work well in international, cross-functional teams. No Drama, Good Karma!

Nice to have
• A CIA, CISA or CFE qualification

• Experience in FinTech

• Experience implementing controls for the first time to support an IPO

• Experience with ERP or system implementations and IT general controls (segregation of duties, access, change management)

About the team and location

You will join a team of professionals based in London and Tallinn, supported by external consultants. Our wider Finance team is spread across the globe, so expect regular video calls. You may also travel once or twice a year for Finance-wide initiatives.

For everyone, everywhere. We're people building money without borders — without judgement or prejudice, too. We believe teams are strongest when they are diverse, equitable and inclusive.
We're proud to have a truly international team, and we celebrate our differences.

Inclusive teams help us live our values and make sure every Wiser feels respected, empowered to contribute towards our mission and able to progress in their careers.
If you want to find out more about what it's like to work at Wise visit Wise.Jobs.
Keep up to date with life at Wise by following us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

About the team
Banks need flexibility in how they fund international payments, settle with Wise and convert currencies. Our Cash Management team builds the products that give them that control and make Wise work for more partners and their customers.
The problems are concrete. How can a bank lock in an exchange rate today and provide the funds later? How can it send payments first and settle with Wise afterward? We build the capabilities behind those choices, helping partners manage their cash around the needs of their business.
We’re a small, growing team developing new products in a domain with plenty to learn and shape. You’ll have a meaningful say in how we solve customer problems, design our systems and maintain engineering quality as we grow. The work combines product development with the challenge of building dependable services that move money across systems.

• Experience operating data assets within a regulated SOX/PCAOB compliance environment.

• Familiarity with cloud data warehouses (e.g., Snowflake) and cloud compute orchestration.

• Prior domain exposure to financial flows, double-entry ledger systems, or accounting integrations.

Soft Skills
• A strong sense of long-term technical ownership.

• Excellent communication skills with the ability to bridge technical engineering realities with financial analyst requirements.
